DigitalOcean calls are sequential within each CLI worker. On HTTP 429 or 503, the client uses `Retry-After` and quota reset headers for bounded retries. If the indicated wait exceeds two minutes or repeated attempts fail, the command stops with `InferencePaused`; completed entries remain committed and a later rerun resumes them. Profile inference releases its database read transaction before calling the model and retries the atomic profile/usage write after a database restart without rerunning the model when the result was already committed. The client also checks the daily tokens remaining in successful response headers before the next request and pauses at `MGRAPH_DO_DAILY_RESERVE_TOKENS` (default 100,000), allowing for estimated prompt and completion tokens. This is a best-effort per-process guard because other account workloads and workers can consume the same allowance. Check live model-specific headers and observe 429s before increasing parallelism beyond two workers. DigitalOcean's published Tier 4 ceiling is higher than the model-specific limits actually returned by the API.

`neighbors --entry node:<id>` returns the currently judged proximity order. User corrections can be recorded with `feedback-pair --left ... --right ... --score 0.9 --label same_niche` and `feedback-order --anchor ... --closer ... --farther ...`. Feedback is stored separately from model judgments and applied when returning neighbors. For a page that requires the authenticated Aside browser, pipe its extracted text into `import-text --entry node:<id> --source-node node:<id>`; this puts the text in R2 and the projection without making a local data file.

`python3 -m mgraph evaluate` runs four fixed synthetic relation cases against GLM-5.3 and Kimi K3 and writes `evaluation.json`. This checks JSON validity, evidence IDs, proximity ordering, latency, and token cost. It is a smoke test, not a labeled corpus evaluation. A user-reviewed test set from actual Memotron entries is still needed before treating the scores as accuracy measurements.

`python3 -m mgraph.evaluate_alternatives` runs the same synthetic cases against other DigitalOcean-hosted models and writes `alternative-evaluation.json`. Valid previous results are retained on rerun, so malformed outputs can be retried with a larger output budget without repeating successful calls. The comparison and whole-account cost scenarios are in `EVALUATION.md`.

The media extractor reads only S3 URLs in the configured user's legacy `tidyfiles` bucket. DynamoDB uses `MGRAPH_SOURCE_AWS_PROFILE`; file reads use `MGRAPH_SOURCE_S3_AWS_PROFILE`, which defaults to the DynamoDB profile. The available `data` profile passed a one-byte object read and is configured for this pilot. The extractor prefers an optional OpenAI-compatible Whisper endpoint on a DigitalOcean GPU Droplet when `MGRAPH_DO_TRANSCRIPTION_URL` is set; otherwise it uses Cloudflare Workers AI Whisper Large V3 Turbo with voice activity filtering. Large audio files are decoded with FFmpeg in memory and transcribed in four-minute chunks; this path requires `ffmpeg` on `PATH`. The DO serverless model catalog currently has no dedicated transcription endpoint. Image-only PDFs fall back to in-memory page rendering and DigitalOcean vision OCR for documents up to 20 pages. Existing transcripts and source metadata are also indexed.

Extraction has visible bounds: 260,000 characters for an HTML page, 100 pages and 260,000 characters for selectable PDF text, 20 pages for scanned PDF OCR, 80 MB for audio, and 30 MB for each PDF or image. Large raster images and GIF first frames are resized in memory before vision inference. Oversized sources keep their metadata in the R2 DynamoDB snapshot and their original bytes in legacy S3; each gets an `extraction_failure` row. Two earlier 80,000-character extracts that were found to be incomplete are marked `partial` and excluded from profiling and rich-evidence counts. Three saved PDFs are 262, 274, and 613 pages; they need a separate book-scale chapter projection before their full text can be profiled without losing coverage. Voice activity filtering can return no words on very short or non-speech audio, which is recorded as an empty-extraction failure.

## Pilot validation

The September 27, 2026 source backfill stored 37,917 records across 80 R2 pages; PostgreSQL record count and page row totals match. The root resolver handles the legacy `$NONE` sentinel, reciprocal page/clip references, and missing parent nodes; the corrected projection contains 5,017 top-level entries. # m graph pilot evaluation

Measured September 27, 2026. The four fixed cases in `evaluation.json` test output shape, evidence IDs, coarse relation labels, and proximity ordering. They are synthetic and too small to estimate production accuracy. The real-account comparison used saved Orca and Synara pages after public-page extraction and GLM-5.3 profiling.

| Model | Fixed labels | Ordering | Fixed-call time | Estimated fixed-call cost | Real Orca/Synara relation |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| GLM-5.3 | 3/4 | pass | 22.44 s | $0.004182 | `same_product`, 0.90 on the final profile format |
| Kimi K3 | 4/4 | pass | 41.86 s | $0.028485 | `same_niche`, 0.87 on the final profile format |

GLM called the synthetic ADE pair `same_product` instead of `same_niche`, though it ranked that pair closer than a general coding IDE. It also called the real saved Orca and Synara pages `same_product` in the final comparison. Kimi distinguished `same_niche` in both. On the final profile format, GLM took 10.49 seconds and approximately $0.00465, including cached input; Kimi took 17.4 seconds and approximately $0.01844. Output token counts and latency vary between requests; these figures are observations, not guarantees.

The pilot should use GLM-5.3 for entry profiling and Kimi K3 for pair judgments where the relation label drives graph placement. A cheaper first-pass judge could be introduced after a larger user-reviewed set with hard negatives, cross-medium conceptual echoes, and page-content hallucination checks establishes its recall and error rate. DigitalOcean's [serverless pricing](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/details/pricing/) lists GLM-5.3 at $1.40 per million input tokens and $4.40 per million output tokens, versus Kimi K3 at $3.00 and $15.00. Cached input is billed at lower rates and is recorded separately by the pipeline. After profiling the saved Cursor page, Kimi judged Cursor against both saved ADE pages at 0.62, below the Orca/Synara 0.87 judgment; this is a useful real-account sanity check, not a broad accuracy measure.

At 80 real GLM-5.3 profile calls, the observed average was 2,270 prompt tokens, 1,096 output tokens, and 24.7 seconds. The observed token shape is used for the whole-account estimate below, with cached input separated from uncached input. Long documents, skipped thin media, retries, and rate limits make any full-run forecast uncertain. The pipeline checkpoints every successful entry so larger runs can be resumed and measured in batches.

Three 27,000-31,000-character source entries exercised the long-profile path. Two were profiled with GLM-5.3 after segment splitting and evidence-ID normalization; one required a Kimi K3 profile after repeated malformed GLM JSON. The Kimi call took 241.7 seconds and used 23,916 prompt and 10,926 completion tokens. Current profiles are preserved on ordinary reruns even when a fallback model was used. This case illustrates why the naive whole-account cost and duration estimate does not cover the long tail.

## Whole-account inference sizing

The current snapshot has 5,017 projected entries. The profile gate admits 4,970 with enough available evidence, including 69 already profiled, leaving 4,901. Across 80 successful GLM-5.3 profile calls, mean usage was 2,270 input tokens, including 689 cached, and 1,096 output tokens. At [Kimi K3 pricing](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/details/pricing/) of $3 per million uncached input tokens, $0.30 cached input tokens, and $15 output tokens, applying that *GLM token shape* to Kimi gives $0.02139 per profile or about **$105 for the remaining 4,901**. Kimi's actual output length, failed calls, and long documents can materially change this; the one measured long Kimi profile cost about $0.22.

Across 54 logged Kimi K3 pair judgments, mean usage was 1,857 input tokens, including 90 cached, and 846 output tokens, for **$0.01801 per successful pair** at current rates. That implies about **$180 for 10,000** or **$360 for 20,000** judged pairs. The present 69-profile graph offers 468 candidate pairs at the current retrieval settings; projecting this density to 4,970 profiles yields roughly 34,000 candidate pairs and about **$607 in pair inference**, or **$712 for profiling plus pair inference** before failed calls, long tails, image processing, embeddings, storage, and any source expansion. Candidate density can change as the graph fills, so 34,000 is a sizing scenario rather than a fixed work count. A 10,000-20,000-pair budget gives a roughly $285-$465 successful-call baseline, with additional allowance needed for retries and unusually long entries.

The observed DigitalOcean model response headers showed 360 requests/minute, 3 million tokens/minute, a 180 million-token daily bucket, and about 18 million tokens remaining at the probe time. [Tier 4 publishes ceilings](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/details/limits/) of up to 360 requests/minute and 12 million tokens/minute; actual limits and available capacity can be lower. A single sequential worker has been far below the minute ceilings, while a full graph can consume more than the then-reported daily remainder. The pipeline now uses quota headers, bounded 429/503 retries, a 100,000-token daily reserve, and committed per-entry checkpoints. Run bounded batches, resume after quota recovery, and increase worker count only after observing headers. DigitalOcean [documents continuous quota refill and shared capacity](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/reference/quota-specific-response-headers/), so neither the Tier 4 number nor this snapshot guarantees zero throttling.

DigitalOcean [requires a positive prepaid balance for serverless inference](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/details/pricing/). Its [Startups terms](https://www.digitalocean.com/startups) distinguish DigitalOcean-hosted models from third-party passthrough models for core-credit eligibility, while [prepayment terms](https://www.digitalocean.com/legal/serverless_inference_prepayment) say restricted credits alone do not satisfy the prepayment gate. Confirm the actual award and account balance before a large run; the dollar estimates above are usage costs regardless of credit coverage.

## Other DigitalOcean model candidates

The additional `alternative-evaluation.json` run used the same four synthetic relation cases. It checks parser compatibility and a few distinctions, not production graph quality. Successful cases initially used a 1,100-token output cap; failures were rerun with a 3,500-token cap and, if needed, one 6,000-token retry, so the timing and cost columns are not a controlled head-to-head benchmark. Failed preliminary calls are not included in the listed successful-call costs.

| Model | Exact labels | Valid outputs | Ordering | Successful-call cost | Observation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
| Kimi K2.6 | 4/4 | 4/4 | pass | $0.01956 | Needs `temperature=1`; a repeated cross-medium case changed label between runs. |
| DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 | 3/4 | 4/4 | pass | $0.00354 | Fast; treated the cross-medium echo as `same_niche`. |
| MiMo V2.5 Pro | 3/4 | 4/4 | pass | $0.01379 | Valid with larger output budget; cross-medium label changed on repeat. |
| GLM-5.3 Flash | 3/4 | 4/4 | pass | $0.00042 | Called close ADEs `same_product`. |
| Nemotron 3 Ultra | 3/4 | 4/4 | pass | $0.00378 | Called the cross-medium echo `same_niche`. |
| Qwen 3.5 397B A17B | incomplete | incomplete | unmeasured | unmeasured | The 1,100-token budget produced no JSON; one larger-budget case succeeded, but the remaining run stalled and was stopped. |

All these model IDs are in the current [DigitalOcean catalog](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/details/models/), and their token rates are in [DigitalOcean pricing](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/details/pricing/). Kimi K2.6, DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813, and MiMo V2.5 Pro are the next useful comparisons on a reviewed sample of actual Memotron pairs. GLM-5.3 Flash is worth testing as a low-cost candidate generator. Kimi K3 remains the stronger measured judge for the saved Orca/Synara distinction, but four synthetic cases and a handful of real pairs are insufficient to choose a final model.

In a real cross-medium check, a saved Markdown entry and a web page received a Kimi `same_niche` judgment at 0.72. This supports using embeddings for recall and reasoning for the final relation; it does not establish graph-wide accuracy.

## Transcription economics

The source contains 69 audio nodes with 94.67 recorded minutes. Forty-five lacked a transcript, totaling 72.47 minutes. At Cloudflare's [Whisper Large V3 Turbo rate](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/models/whisper-large-v3-turbo/) of $0.000513 per audio minute, processing every missing recording is approximately **$0.03718**; retranscribing all audio would be approximately **$0.04856**. Billing can differ if duration metadata is inaccurate or clips are split and retried. The Cloudflare pilot pass produced 24 nonempty audio extractions; 21 more returned empty text under voice activity filtering and remain recorded as failures. A silent synthetic WAV probe likewise returned empty text instead of a spurious transcript.

DigitalOcean's [serverless model catalog](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/details/models/) does not list a dedicated ASR model. Nemotron 3 Diarization supplies speaker labels but no words. An optional OpenAI-compatible Whisper endpoint can be hosted on a DO GPU Droplet and selected through `MGRAPH_DO_TRANSCRIPTION_URL`. DO's [GPU Droplet pricing](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/droplets/details/pricing/) starts at $0.76/hour for RTX 4000 and $1.57/hour for L40s; credits may cover that bill, but provisioning and maintaining a GPU endpoint for this account's roughly four cents of missing Cloudflare transcription is more work than the pilot needs. The `data` AWS profile reads the legacy file objects; saved recordings now pass through Cloudflare ASR. Some recordings produced no detected speech under voice activity filtering and remain explicit failures rather than being populated with likely hallucinated words.

If the indicated wait exceeds two minutes or repeated attempts fail, the command stops with `InferencePaused`; completed entries remain committed and a later rerun resumes them. Profile inference releases its database read transaction before calling the model and retries the atomic profile/usage write after a database restart without rerunning the model when the result was already committed. The client also checks the daily tokens remaining in successful response headers before the next request and pauses at `MGRAPH_DO_DAILY_RESERVE_TOKENS` (default 100,000), allowing for estimated prompt and completion tokens. This is a best-effort per-process guard because other account workloads and workers can consume the same allowance. Check live model-specific headers and observe 429s before increasing parallelism beyond two workers. DigitalOcean's published Tier 4 ceiling is higher than the model-specific limits actually returned by the API.

`neighbors --entry node:<id>` returns the currently judged proximity order. User corrections can be recorded with `feedback-pair --left ... --right ... --score 0.9 --label same_niche` and `feedback-order --anchor ... --closer ... --farther ...`. Feedback is stored separately from model judgments and applied when returning neighbors. For a page that requires the authenticated Aside browser, pipe its extracted text into `import-text --entry node:<id> --source-node node:<id>`; this puts the text in R2 and the projection without making a local data file.

`python3 -m mgraph evaluate` runs four fixed synthetic relation cases against GLM-5.3 and Kimi K3 and writes `evaluation.json`. This checks JSON validity, evidence IDs, proximity ordering, latency, and token cost. It is a smoke test, not a labeled corpus evaluation. A user-reviewed test set from actual Memotron entries is still needed before treating the scores as accuracy measurements.

`python3 -m mgraph.evaluate_alternatives` runs the same synthetic cases against other DigitalOcean-hosted models and writes `alternative-evaluation.json`. Valid previous results are retained on rerun, so malformed outputs can be retried with a larger output budget without repeating successful calls. The comparison and whole-account cost scenarios are in `EVALUATION.md`.

The media extractor reads only S3 URLs in the configured user's legacy `tidyfiles` bucket. DynamoDB uses `MGRAPH_SOURCE_AWS_PROFILE`; file reads use `MGRAPH_SOURCE_S3_AWS_PROFILE`, which defaults to the DynamoDB profile. The available `data` profile passed a one-byte object read and is configured for this pilot. DigitalOcean calls are sequential within each CLI worker. On HTTP 429 or 503, the client uses `Retry-After` and quota reset headers for bounded retries. If the indicated wait exceeds two minutes or repeated attempts fail, the command stops with `InferencePaused`; completed entries remain committed and a later rerun resumes them. Profile inference releases its database read transaction before calling the model and retries the atomic profile/usage write after a database restart without rerunning the model when the result was already committed. The client also checks the daily tokens remaining in successful response headers before the next request and pauses at `MGRAPH_DO_DAILY_RESERVE_TOKENS` (default 100,000), allowing for estimated prompt and completion tokens. This is a best-effort per-process guard because other account workloads and workers can consume the same allowance. Check live model-specific headers and observe 429s before increasing parallelism beyond two workers. DigitalOcean's published Tier 4 ceiling is higher than the model-specific limits actually returned by the API.

`neighbors --entry node:<id>` returns the currently judged proximity order. User corrections can be recorded with `feedback-pair --left ... --right ... --score 0.9 --label same_niche` and `feedback-order --anchor ... --closer ... --farther ...`. Feedback is stored separately from model judgments and applied when returning neighbors. For a page that requires the authenticated Aside browser, pipe its extracted text into `import-text --entry node:<id> --source-node node:<id>`; this puts the text in R2 and the projection without making a local data file.

`python3 -m mgraph evaluate` runs four fixed synthetic relation cases against GLM-5.3 and Kimi K3 and writes `evaluation.json`. This checks JSON validity, evidence IDs, proximity ordering, latency, and token cost. It is a smoke test, not a labeled corpus evaluation. A user-reviewed test set from actual Memotron entries is still needed before treating the scores as accuracy measurements.

`python3 -m mgraph.evaluate_alternatives` runs the same synthetic cases against other DigitalOcean-hosted models and writes `alternative-evaluation.json`. Valid previous results are retained on rerun, so malformed outputs can be retried with a larger output budget without repeating successful calls. The comparison and whole-account cost scenarios are in `EVALUATION.md`.

The media extractor reads only S3 URLs in the configured user's legacy `tidyfiles` bucket. DynamoDB uses `MGRAPH_SOURCE_AWS_PROFILE`; file reads use `MGRAPH_SOURCE_S3_AWS_PROFILE`, which defaults to the DynamoDB profile. The available `data` profile passed a one-byte object read and is configured for this pilot. The extractor prefers an optional OpenAI-compatible Whisper endpoint on a DigitalOcean GPU Droplet when `MGRAPH_DO_TRANSCRIPTION_URL` is set; otherwise it uses Cloudflare Workers AI Whisper Large V3 Turbo with voice activity filtering. Large audio files are decoded with FFmpeg in memory and transcribed in four-minute chunks; this path requires `ffmpeg` on `PATH`. The DO serverless model catalog currently has no dedicated transcription endpoint. Image-only PDFs fall back to in-memory page rendering and DigitalOcean vision OCR for documents up to 20 pages. Existing transcripts and source metadata are also indexed.

Extraction has visible bounds: 260,000 characters for an HTML page, 100 pages and 260,000 characters for selectable PDF text, 20 pages for scanned PDF OCR, 80 MB for audio, and 30 MB for each PDF or image. Large raster images and GIF first frames are resized in memory before vision inference. Oversized sources keep their metadata in the R2 DynamoDB snapshot and their original bytes in legacy S3; each gets an `extraction_failure` row. Two earlier 80,000-character extracts that were found to be incomplete are marked `partial` and excluded from profiling and rich-evidence counts. Three saved PDFs are 262, 274, and 613 pages; they need a separate book-scale chapter projection before their full text can be profiled without losing coverage. Voice activity filtering can return no words on very short or non-speech audio, which is recorded as an empty-extraction failure.

## Pilot validation

The September 27, 2026 source backfill stored 37,917 records across 80 R2 pages; PostgreSQL record count and page row totals match. The root resolver handles the legacy `$NONE` sentinel, reciprocal page/clip references, and missing parent nodes; the corrected projection contains 5,017 top-level entries. R2 page 20 passed a decompression and SHA-256 check. A source audit found four formerly shortened blocks across three entries; all three were reprojected with full source text and profiled. Public-page extraction covered 2,302 of 2,551 web nodes. Media extraction recorded 235 image, 24 audio, and 26 PDF results; one web and one PDF result are marked partial and excluded from profiles. There are 250 web, 11 image, 21 audio, and 5 PDF failure rows, including records that overlap those partial results. The `data` AWS profile read legacy file objects, and saved audio, image, and PDF passed the complete S3-to-R2 extraction path. The inference sample has 69 profiles, 69 embeddings, and 53 judged relations, all current against their profile evidence. A full map of all 5,017 entries still requires a larger inference run. In one cross-medium sample, a saved Markdown entry and a web page received a `same_niche` relation at 0.72, while two high-vector-similarity pairs were judged 0.05 and 0.08; this is a concrete check of the candidate-and-judge split, not an accuracy benchmark.

## Configuration

Fill the remaining blanks in the ignored `.env` in this directory. `.env.example` documents every setting. Do not put credentials in the example file.

- `MGRAPH_DATABASE_URL`: a hosted PostgreSQL connection string with TLS. Use a dedicated database or schema; the provider must support `pgvector`.
- `MGRAPH_DO_MODEL_ACCESS_KEY`: a DigitalOcean serverless inference model access key. The listed reasoning and vision models are starting choices to benchmark.
- `MGRAPH_DO_PROFILE_REASONING_EFFORT` and `MGRAPH_DO_IDENTITY_REASONING_EFFORT`: reasoning effort for Kimi profile extraction and selective web identity judgments; both default to `low` in the pilot. `MGRAPH_DO_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` bounds each model request.
- `MGRAPH_DO_PROFILE_MODEL`, `MGRAPH_DO_RELATION_MODEL`, and `MGRAPH_DO_VISION_MODEL`: select Kimi K3 for profiles, pair judgments, and image understanding in the full pilot. The earlier GLM and Nemotron results remain in the evaluation history.
- `MGRAPH_CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `MGRAPH_CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_AI_API_TOKEN`: Workers AI REST access for embeddings and transcription.
- `MGRAPH_R2_BUCKET`, `MGRAPH_R2_ENDPOINT`, `MGRAPH_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, and `MGRAPH_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`: a private bucket and bucket-scoped S3 API credentials with object read/write access. R2 credentials are distinct from the Workers AI token.
- `MGRAPH_SOURCE_AWS_PROFILE`, `MGRAPH_SOURCE_S3_AWS_PROFILE`, `MGRAPH_SOURCE_AWS_REGION`, `MGRAPH_SOURCE_DYNAMODB_TABLE`, and `MGRAPH_SOURCE_USER_ID`: identify the read-only source and its separate file-read identity.

For the standard R2 jurisdiction, the endpoint is `https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`. A jurisdictional bucket needs its matching endpoint. Keep the bucket private. The backfill will use account-scoped object keys beneath `MGRAPH_R2_PREFIX` and keep object hashes and job checkpoints in PostgreSQL.

## Provisioned Cloudflare resource

The 21n Cloudflare account has a dedicated `mgraph-pilot` R2 bucket in the APAC location. Its `r2.dev` public URL is disabled and it has no custom domains. The account ID, bucket, endpoint, and user-scoped object prefix are already set in the local `.env`.

The local `.env` contains a [bucket-scoped R2 Object Read & Write S3 key pair](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/api/tokens/) for `mgraph-pilot` and a separate [Workers AI API token](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/get-started/rest-api/). The R2 user token expires on September 27, 2027.

## Connection checks

On September 27, 2026, hosted PostgreSQL, `pgvector` migration, R2 read/write, 1,024-dimensional Workers AI embeddings, DigitalOcean reasoning and vision, and Cloudflare transcription all passed live pilot checks. The hosted database schema was also tested by applying the migration to a rolled-back scratch schema. The source snapshot and extraction artifacts are stored in private R2, not on local disk.

The pilot will never write to the legacy DynamoDB table. Its snapshot is a fixed input to a derived graph; later catch-up and the DataFn migration are separate work.
# m graph pilot evaluation

Measured September 27, 2026. The four fixed cases in `evaluation.json` test output shape, evidence IDs, coarse relation labels, and proximity ordering. They are synthetic and too small to estimate production accuracy. The real-account comparison used saved Orca and Synara pages after public-page extraction and GLM-5.3 profiling.

| Model | Fixed labels | Ordering | Fixed-call time | Estimated fixed-call cost | Real Orca/Synara relation |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| GLM-5.3 | 3/4 | pass | 22.44 s | $0.004182 | `same_product`, 0.90 on the final profile format |
| Kimi K3 | 4/4 | pass | 41.86 s | $0.028485 | `same_niche`, 0.87 on the final profile format |

GLM called the synthetic ADE pair `same_product` instead of `same_niche`, though it ranked that pair closer than a general coding IDE. It also called the real saved Orca and Synara pages `same_product` in the final comparison. Kimi distinguished `same_niche` in both. On the final profile format, GLM took 10.49 seconds and approximately $0.00465, including cached input; Kimi took 17.4 seconds and approximately $0.01844. Output token counts and latency vary between requests; these figures are observations, not guarantees.

The pilot should use GLM-5.3 for entry profiling and Kimi K3 for pair judgments where the relation label drives graph placement. A cheaper first-pass judge could be introduced after a larger user-reviewed set with hard negatives, cross-medium conceptual echoes, and page-content hallucination checks establishes its recall and error rate. DigitalOcean's [serverless pricing](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/details/pricing/) lists GLM-5.3 at $1.40 per million input tokens and $4.40 per million output tokens, versus Kimi K3 at $3.00 and $15.00. Cached input is billed at lower rates and is recorded separately by the pipeline. After profiling the saved Cursor page, Kimi judged Cursor against both saved ADE pages at 0.62, below the Orca/Synara 0.87 judgment; this is a useful real-account sanity check, not a broad accuracy measure.

At 80 real GLM-5.3 profile calls, the observed average was 2,270 prompt tokens, 1,096 output tokens, and 24.7 seconds. The observed token shape is used for the whole-account estimate below, with cached input separated from uncached input. Long documents, skipped thin media, retries, and rate limits make any full-run forecast uncertain. The pipeline checkpoints every successful entry so larger runs can be resumed and measured in batches.

Three 27,000-31,000-character source entries exercised the long-profile path. Two were profiled with GLM-5.3 after segment splitting and evidence-ID normalization; one required a Kimi K3 profile after repeated malformed GLM JSON. The Kimi call took 241.7 seconds and used 23,916 prompt and 10,926 completion tokens. Current profiles are preserved on ordinary reruns even when a fallback model was used. This case illustrates why the naive whole-account cost and duration estimate does not cover the long tail.

## Whole-account inference sizing

The current snapshot has 5,017 projected entries. The profile gate admits 4,970 with enough available evidence, including 69 already profiled, leaving 4,901. Across 80 successful GLM-5.3 profile calls, mean usage was 2,270 input tokens, including 689 cached, and 1,096 output tokens. At [Kimi K3 pricing](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/details/pricing/) of $3 per million uncached input tokens, $0.30 cached input tokens, and $15 output tokens, applying that *GLM token shape* to Kimi gives $0.02139 per profile or about **$105 for the remaining 4,901**. Kimi's actual output length, failed calls, and long documents can materially change this; the one measured long Kimi profile cost about $0.22.

Across 54 logged Kimi K3 pair judgments, mean usage was 1,857 input tokens, including 90 cached, and 846 output tokens, for **$0.01801 per successful pair** at current rates. That implies about **$180 for 10,000** or **$360 for 20,000** judged pairs. The present 69-profile graph offers 468 candidate pairs at the current retrieval settings; projecting this density to 4,970 profiles yields roughly 34,000 candidate pairs and about **$607 in pair inference**, or **$712 for profiling plus pair inference** before failed calls, long tails, image processing, embeddings, storage, and any source expansion. Candidate density can change as the graph fills, so 34,000 is a sizing scenario rather than a fixed work count. A 10,000-20,000-pair budget gives a roughly $285-$465 successful-call baseline, with additional allowance needed for retries and unusually long entries.

The observed DigitalOcean model response headers showed 360 requests/minute, 3 million tokens/minute, a 180 million-token daily bucket, and about 18 million tokens remaining at the probe time. [Tier 4 publishes ceilings](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/details/limits/) of up to 360 requests/minute and 12 million tokens/minute; actual limits and available capacity can be lower. A single sequential worker has been far below the minute ceilings, while a full graph can consume more than the then-reported daily remainder. The pipeline now uses quota headers, bounded 429/503 retries, a 100,000-token daily reserve, and committed per-entry checkpoints. Run bounded batches, resume after quota recovery, and increase worker count only after observing headers. DigitalOcean [documents continuous quota refill and shared capacity](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/reference/quota-specific-response-headers/), so neither the Tier 4 number nor this snapshot guarantees zero throttling.

DigitalOcean [requires a positive prepaid balance for serverless inference](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/details/pricing/). Its [Startups terms](https://www.digitalocean.com/startups) distinguish DigitalOcean-hosted models from third-party passthrough models for core-credit eligibility, while [prepayment terms](https://www.digitalocean.com/legal/serverless_inference_prepayment) say restricted credits alone do not satisfy the prepayment gate. Confirm the actual award and account balance before a large run; the dollar estimates above are usage costs regardless of credit coverage.

## Other DigitalOcean model candidates

The additional `alternative-evaluation.json` run used the same four synthetic relation cases. It checks parser compatibility and a few distinctions, not production graph quality. Successful cases initially used a 1,100-token output cap; failures were rerun with a 3,500-token cap and, if needed, one 6,000-token retry, so the timing and cost columns are not a controlled head-to-head benchmark. Failed preliminary calls are not included in the listed successful-call costs.

| Model | Exact labels | Valid outputs | Ordering | Successful-call cost | Observation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
| Kimi K2.6 | 4/4 | 4/4 | pass | $0.01956 | Needs `temperature=1`; a repeated cross-medium case changed label between runs. |
| DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 | 3/4 | 4/4 | pass | $0.00354 | Fast; treated the cross-medium echo as `same_niche`. |
| MiMo V2.5 Pro | 3/4 | 4/4 | pass | $0.01379 | Valid with larger output budget; cross-medium label changed on repeat. |
| GLM-5.3 Flash | 3/4 | 4/4 | pass | $0.00042 | Called close ADEs `same_product`. |
| Nemotron 3 Ultra | 3/4 | 4/4 | pass | $0.00378 | Called the cross-medium echo `same_niche`. |
| Qwen 3.5 397B A17B | incomplete | incomplete | unmeasured | unmeasured | The 1,100-token budget produced no JSON; one larger-budget case succeeded, but the remaining run stalled and was stopped. |

All these model IDs are in the current [DigitalOcean catalog](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/details/models/), and their token rates are in [DigitalOcean pricing](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/details/pricing/). Kimi K2.6, DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813, and MiMo V2.5 Pro are the next useful comparisons on a reviewed sample of actual Memotron pairs. GLM-5.3 Flash is worth testing as a low-cost candidate generator. Kimi K3 remains the stronger measured judge for the saved Orca/Synara distinction, but four synthetic cases and a handful of real pairs are insufficient to choose a final model.

In a real cross-medium check, a saved Markdown entry and a web page received a Kimi `same_niche` judgment at 0.72. Two other vector-nearest candidates for long entries scored 0.05 and 0.08 after pair judgment. This supports using embeddings for recall and reasoning for the final relation; it does not establish graph-wide accuracy.

## Transcription economics

The source contains 69 audio nodes with 94.67 recorded minutes. Forty-five lacked a transcript, totaling 72.47 minutes. At Cloudflare's [Whisper Large V3 Turbo rate](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/models/whisper-large-v3-turbo/) of $0.000513 per audio minute, processing every missing recording is approximately **$0.03718**; retranscribing all audio would be approximately **$0.04856**. Billing can differ if duration metadata is inaccurate or clips are split and retried. The Cloudflare pilot pass produced 24 nonempty audio extractions; 21 more returned empty text under voice activity filtering and remain recorded as failures. A silent synthetic WAV probe likewise returned empty text instead of a spurious transcript.

DigitalOcean's [serverless model catalog](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/details/models/) does not list a dedicated ASR model. Nemotron 3 Diarization supplies speaker labels but no words. An optional OpenAI-compatible Whisper endpoint can be hosted on a DO GPU Droplet and selected through `MGRAPH_DO_TRANSCRIPTION_URL`. DO's [GPU Droplet pricing](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/droplets/details/pricing/) starts at $0.76/hour for RTX 4000 and $1.57/hour for L40s; credits may cover that bill, but provisioning and maintaining a GPU endpoint for this account's roughly four cents of missing Cloudflare transcription is more work than the pilot needs. The `data` AWS profile reads the legacy file objects; saved recordings now pass through Cloudflare ASR. Some recordings produced no detected speech under voice activity filtering and remain explicit failures rather than being populated with likely hallucinated words.

"""Read-only queries shared by the local MCP server and map prototype."""
import heapq
import json
import threading
import time

from .cli import apply_order_feedback, config, database, text_parts
from .profile_quality import normalize_property_key


def accepted_extraction(schema, alias="x"):
    """Use web text only after its saved-page identity was screened."""
    return f"(left({alias}.kind,4)<>'web:' OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM {schema}.web_identity w JOIN {schema}.source_record n ON n.resource='node' AND n.id=substring({alias}.kind from 5) WHERE w.entry_id={alias}.entry_id AND w.kind={alias}.kind AND w.status='accepted' AND w.saved_hash=n.sha256 AND w.extraction_updated_at={alias}.updated_at))"


GRAPH_THRESHOLD = 0.65
SOURCE_RESOURCES = ("node", "file", "link", "collection", "property", "linkTag")
_graph_cache = {"at": 0.0, "value": None}
_graph_lock = threading.Lock()


def _graph_index():
    """Cache compact graph topology so map pages never fetch all node profiles."""
    with _graph_lock:
        if _graph_cache["value"] is not None and time.monotonic() - _graph_cache["at"] < 30:
            return _graph_cache["value"]
        schema = config()
        with database() as conn:
            profiled = {row[0] for row in conn.execute(f"SELECT entry_id FROM {schema}.profile")}
            relation_rows = conn.execute(f"SELECT left_id,right_id,score,judgment->>'relation' FROM {schema}.relation").fetchall()
            feedback_rows = conn.execute(f"SELECT left_id,right_id,score,label FROM {schema}.pair_feedback").fetchall()
            total = conn.execute(f"SELECT count(*) FROM {schema}.entry").fetchone()[0]
        edges = {}
        for left, right, score, relation in relation_rows:
            if left in profiled and right in profiled:
                key = tuple(sorted((left, right)))
                edges[key] = {"left": key[0], "right": key[1], "score": score, "relation": relation, "feedback": False}
        for left, right, score, relation in feedback_rows:
            if left in profiled and right in profiled:
                key = tuple(sorted((left, right)))
                edges[key] = {"left": key[0], "right": key[1], "score": score, "relation": relation, "feedback": True}
        adjacency = {}
        for edge in edges.values():
            if edge["score"] < GRAPH_THRESHOLD:
                continue
            adjacency.setdefault(edge["left"], []).append((edge["right"], edge["score"]))
            adjacency.setdefault(edge["right"], []).append((edge["left"], edge["score"]))
        seen = set()
        groups = []
        for start in sorted(adjacency):
            if start in seen:
                continue
            pending = [start]
            members = set()
            while pending:
                current = pending.pop()
                if current in seen:
                    continue
                seen.add(current)
                members.add(current)
                pending.extend(other for other, _ in adjacency[current] if other not in seen)
            root = max(members, key=lambda item: (sum(score for _, score in adjacency[item]), -len(item), item))
            traversal = [root]
            parents = {root: None}
            frontier = [(-score, root, other) for other, score in adjacency[root]]
            heapq.heapify(frontier)
            while frontier:
                negative_score, parent, child = heapq.heappop(frontier)
                if child in parents:
                    continue
                parents[child] = parent
                traversal.append(child)
                for other, score in adjacency[child]:
                    if other not in parents:
                        heapq.heappush(frontier, (-score, child, other))
            groups.append({"id": min(members), "size": len(members), "anchor": root, "members": traversal, "parents": parents})
        groups.sort(key=lambda group: (-group["size"], group["id"]))
        value = {"groups": groups, "edges": edges, "total_entries": total, "profiled_entries": len(profiled)}
        _graph_cache.update(at=time.monotonic(), value=value)
        return value


def map_groups(offset=0, limit=8):
    """Return one page of connected proximity groups and map coverage."""
    graph = _graph_index()
    offset = max(0, int(offset))
    limit = max(1, min(int(limit), 20))
    groups = graph["groups"][offset:offset + limit]
    return {"total_entries": graph["total_entries"], "profiled_entries": graph["profiled_entries"], "connected_entries": sum(group["size"] for group in graph["groups"]), "group_count": len(graph["groups"]), "offset": offset, "next_offset": offset + limit if offset + limit < len(graph["groups"]) else None, "groups": [{"id": group["id"], "size": group["size"], "anchor": group["anchor"]} for group in groups]}


def map_group(group_id, page=0, page_size=24):
    """Return a bounded connected slice, with bridge nodes for page boundaries."""
    graph = _graph_index()
    group = next((item for item in graph["groups"] if item["id"] == group_id), None)
    if group is None:
        return None
    page = max(0, int(page))
    page_size = max(2, min(int(page_size), 32))
    selected = group["members"][page * page_size:(page + 1) * page_size]
    context = {group["parents"][item] for item in selected if group["parents"][item] and group["parents"][item] not in selected}
    ids = selected + sorted(context)
    if not ids:
        return {"id": group_id, "size": group["size"], "page": page, "page_size": page_size, "pages": (group["size"] + page_size - 1) // page_size, "nodes": [], "edges": [], "order_feedback": []}
    schema = config()
    with database() as conn:
        rows = conn.execute(f"SELECT e.id,e.label,e.content_type,e.evidence_quality,p.profile FROM {schema}.entry e JOIN {schema}.profile p ON p.entry_id=e.id WHERE e.id=ANY(%s)", (ids,)).fetchall()
        rules = conn.execute(f"SELECT anchor_id,closer_id,farther_id FROM {schema}.order_feedback WHERE anchor_id=ANY(%s) AND closer_id=ANY(%s) AND farther_id=ANY(%s)", (ids, ids, ids)).fetchall()
    id_set = set(ids)
    context_set = set(context)
    nodes = [{"id": row[0], "label": row[1], "type": row[2], "quality": row[3], "concepts": row[4].get("concepts", [])[:5], "tags": row[4].get("tags", [])[:5], "context": row[0] in context_set} for row in rows]
    edges = [edge for edge in graph["edges"].values() if edge["score"] >= GRAPH_THRESHOLD and edge["left"] in id_set and edge["right"] in id_set]
    return {"id": group_id, "size": group["size"], "page": page, "page_size": page_size, "pages": (group["size"] + page_size - 1) // page_size, "nodes": nodes, "edges": edges, "order_feedback": [{"anchor": row[0], "closer": row[1], "farther": row[2]} for row in rules]}


def library_resources():
    """Count authoritative source records by legacy Memotron resource."""
    schema = config()
    with database() as conn:
        counts = dict(conn.execute(f"SELECT resource,count(*) FROM {schema}.source_record GROUP BY resource").fetchall())
    return [{"resource": resource, "count": counts.get(resource, 0)} for resource in SOURCE_RESOURCES]


def library_records(resource, page=0, page_size=30, search=""):
    """Page authoritative records with compact projection status for list rendering."""
    if resource not in SOURCE_RESOURCES:
        raise ValueError("Unknown resource")
    page = max(0, int(page))
    page_size = max(1, min(int(page_size), 50))
    search = search.strip()[:200]
    schema = config()
    condition = "s.resource=%s"
    args = [resource]
    if search:
        condition += " AND (s.id ILIKE %s OR s.payload->>'label' ILIKE %s OR s.payload->>'url' ILIKE %s OR s.payload->>'text' ILIKE %s OR s.payload->>'body' ILIKE %s)"
        args.extend([f"%{search}%"] * 5)
    with database() as conn:
        total = conn.execute(f"SELECT count(*) FROM {schema}.source_record s WHERE {condition}", args).fetchone()[0]
        rows = conn.execute(f"SELECT s.id,s.payload,s.ingested_at,e.evidence_quality,p.entry_id IS NOT NULL,v.entry_id IS NOT NULL FROM {schema}.source_record s LEFT JOIN {schema}.entry e ON s.resource='node' AND e.id=s.id LEFT JOIN {schema}.profile p ON p.entry_id=e.id LEFT JOIN {schema}.embedding v ON v.entry_id=e.id WHERE {condition} ORDER BY s.payload->>'modifiedAt' DESC NULLS LAST,s.id LIMIT %s OFFSET %s", (*args, page_size, page * page_size)).fetchall()
    records = []
    for record_id, payload, ingested_at, quality, profiled, embedded in rows:
        prose = " ".join(text_parts(payload.get("text")) + text_parts(payload.get("body")) + text_parts(payload.get("metadata"))).strip()
        prose = " ".join(prose.split())
        label = payload.get("label")
        if not isinstance(label, str) or not label.strip():
        rows = conn.execute(f"WITH needle AS (SELECT plainto_tsquery('english',%s) AS tsq) SELECT e.id,e.label,e.content_type,CASE WHEN e.evidence_quality='rich' OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM {schema}.extraction x WHERE x.entry_id=e.id AND NOT x.partial AND {accepted} AND length(x.text_content)>=400) THEN 'rich' ELSE e.evidence_quality END,p.profile IS NOT NULL AS profiled,ts_rank(to_tsvector('english',coalesce(e.label,'') || ' ' || e.evidence_text),n.tsq) AS rank FROM {schema}.entry e LEFT JOIN {schema}.profile p ON p.entry_id=e.id CROSS JOIN needle n WHERE e.id ILIKE %s OR e.label ILIKE %s OR to_tsvector('english',coalesce(e.label,'') || ' ' || e.evidence_text) @@ n.tsq OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM {schema}.extraction x WHERE x.entry_id=e.id AND NOT x.partial AND {accepted} AND to_tsvector('english',x.text_content) @@ n.tsq) ORDER BY rank DESC,e.label NULLS LAST,e.id LIMIT %s", (query, f"%{query}%", f"%{query}%", limit)).fetchall()
    return [{"id": row[0], "label": row[1], "content_type": row[2], "evidence_quality": row[3], "profiled": row[4], "rank": float(row[5])} for row in rows]


def get_entry(entry_id, max_chars=12000, include_quarantined=True):
    """Return source-cited evidence, extracted media, and the current profile."""
    schema = config()
    max_chars = max(100, min(int(max_chars), 40000))
    accepted = accepted_extraction(schema)
    with database() as conn:
        row = conn.execute(f"SELECT e.id,e.label,e.content_type,e.url,CASE WHEN e.evidence_quality='rich' OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM {schema}.extraction x WHERE x.entry_id=e.id AND NOT x.partial AND {accepted} AND length(x.text_content)>=400) THEN 'rich' ELSE e.evidence_quality END,e.evidence_text,e.evidence_refs,p.profile,p.model FROM {schema}.entry e LEFT JOIN {schema}.profile p ON p.entry_id=e.id WHERE e.id=%s", (entry_id,)).fetchone()
        if not row:
            return None

            feedback_rows = conn.execute(f"SELECT left_id,right_id,score,label FROM {schema}.pair_feedback").fetchall()
            total = conn.execute(f"SELECT count(*) FROM {schema}.entry").fetchone()[0]
        edges = {}
        for left, right, score, relation in relation_rows:

        adjacency = {}
        for edge in edges.values():
            if edge["score"] < GRAPH_THRESHOLD:

def map_group(group_id, page=0, page_size=24):
    """Return a bounded connected slice, with bridge nodes for page boundaries."""
    graph = _graph_index()
    group = next((item for item in graph["groups"] if item["id"] == group_id), None)
    if group is None:
        return None
    page = max(0, int(page))
    page_size = max(2, min(int(page_size), 32))
    selected = group["members"][page * page_size:(page + 1) * page_size]
    context = {group["parents"][item] for item in selected if group["parents"][item] and group["parents"][item] not in selected}
    ids = selected + sorted(context)
    if not ids:
        return {"id": group_id, "size": group["size"], "page": page, "page_size": page_size, "pages": (group["size"] + page_size - 1) // page_size, "nodes": [], "edges": [], "order_feedback": []}
    schema = config()
    with database() as conn:
        rows = conn.execute(f"SELECT e.id,e.label,e.content_type,e.evidence_quality,p.profile FROM {schema}.entry e JOIN {schema}.profile p ON p.entry_id=e.id WHERE e.id=ANY(%s)", (ids,)).fetchall()
        rules = conn.execute(f"SELECT anchor_id,closer_id,farther_id FROM {schema}.order_feedback WHERE anchor_id=ANY(%s) AND closer_id=ANY(%s) AND farther_id=ANY(%s)", (ids, ids, ids)).fetchall()
    id_set = set(ids)
    context_set = set(context)
    nodes = [{"id": row[0], "label": row[1], "type": row[2], "quality": row[3], "concepts": row[4].get("concepts", [])[:5], "tags": row[4].get("tags", [])[:5], "context": row[0] in context_set} for row in rows]

    return {"id": group_id, "size": group["size"], "page": page, "page_size": page_size, "pages": (group["size"] + page_size - 1) // page_size, "nodes": nodes, "edges": edges, "order_feedback": [{"anchor": row[0], "closer": row[1], "farther": row[2]} for row in rules]}

        ranked = {other: {"id": other, "score": score, "relation": relation, "label": label} for other, score, relation, label in rows}
        for left, right, score, label in conn.execute(f"SELECT left_id,right_id,score,label FROM {schema}.pair_feedback WHERE left_id=%s OR right_id=%s", (entry_id, entry_id)):

def save_profile(schema, entry_id, combined_hash, model, result, embedding_text, usage, latency):
    """Persist an inferred profile atomically, reconnecting after database restarts."""
    for attempt in range(8):
        try:
            with database() as conn:
                conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO {schema}.profile(entry_id,source_hash,model,profile,text_for_embedding,prompt_version) VALUES (%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s) ON CONFLICT(entry_id) DO UPDATE SET source_hash=excluded.source_hash,model=excluded.model,profile=excluded.profile,text_for_embedding=excluded.text_for_embedding,prompt_version=excluded.prompt_version,updated_at=now()", (entry_id, combined_hash, model, Jsonb(result), embedding_text, PROFILE_VERSION))
                conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO {schema}.inference_call(stage,target_key,model,input_tokens,cached_input_tokens,output_tokens,seconds) VALUES (%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s)", ("profile", entry_id, model, usage.get("prompt_tokens", 0), usage.get("cache_read_input_tokens", 0), usage.get("completion_tokens", 0), latency))
            return
        except (psycopg.OperationalError, psycopg.InterfaceError):
            try:
                with database() as conn:
                    persisted = conn.execute(f"SELECT source_hash,model,prompt_version FROM {schema}.profile WHERE entry_id=%s", (entry_id,)).fetchone()
                if persisted == (combined_hash, model, PROFILE_VERSION):
                    return
            except (psycopg.OperationalError, psycopg.InterfaceError):
                pass
            if attempt == 7:
                raise
            time.sleep(min(2 ** attempt, 30))


def profile(schema, limit, model, entry_ids=None, shard=0, shards=1, force_model=False):
    """Derive versioned profiles from source and extraction evidence."""
    from .web_identity import pending_count
    pending = pending_count(schema)
    if pending:
        raise ValueError(f"{pending} web extractions need identity screening before profiling")
    effort = os.environ.get("MGRAPH_DO_PROFILE_REASONING_EFFORT", "low" if model == "kimi-k3" else "")
    if effort:
        os.environ["MGRAPH_DO_REASONING_EFFORT"] = effort
    with database() as conn:
        rows = conn.execute(f"SELECT e.id,e.content_type,e.label,e.evidence_text,e.source_hash,e.evidence_refs,coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('kind',x.kind,'text',x.text_content,'observed_at',x.updated_at::text) ORDER BY x.kind) FILTER (WHERE x.kind IS NOT NULL),'[]'::jsonb) AS extractions,p.source_hash,p.prompt_version,p.model FROM {schema}.entry e LEFT JOIN {schema}.extraction x ON x.entry_id=e.id AND NOT x.partial AND (left(x.kind,4)<>'web:' OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM {schema}.web_identity w JOIN {schema}.source_record n ON n.resource='node' AND n.id=substring(x.kind from 5) WHERE w.entry_id=x.entry_id AND w.kind=x.kind AND w.status='accepted' AND w.saved_hash=n.sha256 AND w.extraction_updated_at=x.updated_at)) LEFT JOIN {schema}.profile p ON p.entry_id=e.id GROUP BY e.id,p.source_hash,p.prompt_version,p.model ORDER BY e.id").fetchall()
    completed = 0
    for entry_id, kind, label, source_text, source_hash, evidence_refs, extractions, old_hash, old_version, old_model in rows:
        if entry_ids and entry_id not in entry_ids:
            continue
        if int(sha(entry_id)[:8], 16) % shards != shard:
            continue
        extracted = "\n".join(item["text"] for item in extractions)
        if kind in ("AUDIO", "IMAGE", "PDF", "VIDEO") and not extracted and len(source_text) < 400:
            continue
        content = (source_text + "\n" + extracted).strip()
        combined_hash = sha(source_hash + sha(extracted))
        if len(content) < 40 or (combined_hash == old_hash and old_version == PROFILE_VERSION and (old_model == model or not force_model)):
            continue
        try:
            allowed_ids = {entry_id} | {ref["id"] for ref in evidence_refs}
            result, usage, latency = derive_profile(model, entry_id, kind, source_text, allowed_ids, extractions)
            if not valid_profile(result):
                result, retry_usage, retry_latency = derive_profile(model, entry_id, kind, source_text, allowed_ids, extractions)
                usage = {"prompt_tokens": usage.get("prompt_tokens", 0) + retry_usage.get("prompt_tokens", 0), "cache_read_input_tokens": usage.get("cache_read_input_tokens", 0) + retry_usage.get("cache_read_input_tokens", 0), "completion_tokens": usage.get("completion_tokens", 0) + retry_usage.get("completion_tokens", 0)}
                latency += retry_latency
            if not valid_profile(result):
                raise ValueError("invalid profile shape")
            result = anchor_saved_name(result, entry_id, label, build_passages(entry_id, source_text, extractions))
            valid_claims = [claim for claim in result["claims"] if isinstance(claim, dict) and isinstance(claim.get("evidence_id"), str) and claim["evidence_id"] in allowed_ids]
            if len(valid_claims) != len(result["claims"]):
                result["claims"] = valid_claims
                result["uncertainty"].append("Claims without a valid source evidence ID were removed")
            embedding_text = "\n".join(["Saved title: " + str(label or ""), result.get("summary", ""), "Concepts: " + ", ".join(result.get("concepts", [])[:20]), "Tags: " + ", ".join(result.get("tags", [])[:20]), "Claims: " + "; ".join(str(claim.get("text", "")) for claim in result.get("claims", [])[:15])])
            save_profile(schema, entry_id, combined_hash, model, result, embedding_text, usage, latency)
            completed += 1
            print(f"profile {completed}: {entry_id} {latency:.1f}s {usage}", flush=True)
        except (httpx.HTTPError, ValueError, KeyError) as error:
            print(f"profile failed {entry_id}: {type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:150]}", flush=True)
        if limit and completed >= limit:
            break


def cf_embed(content):
    """Generate a 1024-dimensional Workers AI embedding."""
    model = os.environ.get("MGRAPH_CF_EMBEDDING_MODEL", "@cf/qwen/qwen3-embedding-0.6b")
    result = cf_ai_post(model, {"text": [content[:8000]]})

def audit_profiles(schema, model):
    """Block downstream inference until eligible profiles have cited current output."""
    from .web_identity import pending_count
    pending = pending_count(schema)
    if pending:
        raise ValueError(f"{pending} web extractions need identity screening before profile audit")
    with database() as conn:
        rows = conn.execute(f"SELECT e.id,e.content_type,e.label,e.evidence_text,e.source_hash,coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('kind',x.kind,'text',x.text_content,'observed_at',x.updated_at::text) ORDER BY x.kind) FILTER (WHERE x.kind IS NOT NULL),'[]'::jsonb),p.source_hash,p.prompt_version,p.model,p.profile FROM {schema}.entry e LEFT JOIN {schema}.extraction x ON x.entry_id=e.id AND NOT x.partial AND (left(x.kind,4)<>'web:' OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM {schema}.web_identity w JOIN {schema}.source_record n ON n.resource='node' AND n.id=substring(x.kind from 5) WHERE w.entry_id=x.entry_id AND w.kind=x.kind AND w.status='accepted' AND w.saved_hash=n.sha256 AND w.extraction_updated_at=x.updated_at)) LEFT JOIN {schema}.profile p ON p.entry_id=e.id GROUP BY e.id,p.source_hash,p.prompt_version,p.model,p.profile ORDER BY e.id").fetchall()
    eligible = 0
    current = 0
    problems = []
    for entry_id, kind, label, source_text, source_hash, extractions, profile_hash, version, profile_model, result in rows:
        extracted = "\n".join(item["text"] for item in extractions)
        if kind in ("AUDIO", "IMAGE", "PDF", "VIDEO") and not extracted and len(source_text) < 400:
            continue
        if len((source_text + "\n" + extracted).strip()) < 40:
            continue
        eligible += 1
        if not result or profile_hash != sha(source_hash + sha(extracted)) or version != PROFILE_VERSION or profile_model != model:
            problems.append((entry_id, "missing or stale profile"))
            continue
        current += 1
        passages = build_passages(entry_id, source_text, extractions)
        issues = profile_issues(result, passages)
        if label and anchor_saved_name(dict(result), entry_id, label, passages)["properties"].get("name") != result.get("properties", {}).get("name"):
            issues.append("saved title is not the primary name")
        problems.extend((entry_id, issue) for issue in issues)
    print(f"profile audit: {current}/{eligible} current {PROFILE_VERSION} {model} profiles; {len(problems)} issues")
    for entry_id, issue in problems[:10]:
        print(f"profile audit issue {entry_id}: {issue}")
    if problems:
        raise ValueError("profile audit failed; resume or repair profiling before downstream stages")

GRAPH_THRESHOLD = 0.65
SOURCE_RESOURCES = ("node", "file", "link", "collection", "property", "linkTag")
_graph_cache = {"at": 0.0, "value": None}
_graph_lock = threading.Lock()


def _graph_index():
    """Cache compact graph topology so map pages never fetch all node profiles."""
    with _graph_lock:
        if _graph_cache["value"] is not None and time.monotonic() - _graph_cache["at"] < 30:
            return _graph_cache["value"]
        schema = config()
        with database() as conn:
            profiled = {row[0] for row in conn.execute(f"SELECT entry_id FROM {schema}.profile")}
            relation_rows = conn.execute(f"SELECT left_id,right_id,score,judgment->>'relation' FROM {schema}.relation").fetchall()
            feedback_rows = conn.execute(f"SELECT left_id,right_id,score,label FROM {schema}.pair_feedback").fetchall()
            total = conn.execute(f"SELECT count(*) FROM {schema}.entry").fetchone()[0]
        edges = {}
        for left, right, score, relation in relation_rows:
            if left in profiled and right in profiled:
                key = tuple(sorted((left, right)))
                edges[key] = {"left": key[0], "right": key[1], "score": score, "relation": relation, "feedback": False}
        for left, right, score, relation in feedback_rows:
            if left in profiled and right in profiled:
                key = tuple(sorted((left, right)))
                edges[key] = {"left": key[0], "right": key[1], "score": score, "relation": relation, "feedback": True}
        adjacency = {}
        for edge in edges.values():
            if edge["score"] < GRAPH_THRESHOLD:
                continue
            adjacency.setdefault(edge["left"], []).append((edge["right"], edge["score"]))
            adjacency.setdefault(edge["right"], []).append((edge["left"], edge["score"]))
        seen = set()
        groups = []
        for start in sorted(adjacency):
            if start in seen:
                continue
            pending = [start]
            members = set()
            while pending:
                current = pending.pop()
                if current in seen:
                    continue
                seen.add(current)
                members.add(current)
                pending.extend(other for other, _ in adjacency[current] if other not in seen)
            root = max(members, key=lambda item: (sum(score for _, score in adjacency[item]), -len(item), item))
            traversal = [root]
            parents = {root: None}
            frontier = [(-score, root, other) for other, score in adjacency[root]]
            heapq.heapify(frontier)
            while frontier:
                negative_score, parent, child = heapq.heappop(frontier)
                if child in parents:
                    continue
                parents[child] = parent
                traversal.append(child)
                for other, score in adjacency[child]:
                    if other not in parents:
                        heapq.heappush(frontier, (-score, child, other))
            groups.append({"id": min(members), "size": len(members), "anchor": root, "members": traversal, "parents": parents})
        groups.sort(key=lambda group: (-group["size"], group["id"]))
        value = {"groups": groups, "edges": edges, "total_entries": total, "profiled_entries": len(profiled)}
        _graph_cache.update(at=time.monotonic(), value=value)
        return value

def map_group(group_id, page=0, page_size=24):
    """Return a bounded connected slice, with bridge nodes for page boundaries."""
    graph = _graph_index()
    group = next((item for item in graph["groups"] if item["id"] == group_id), None)
    if group is None:
        return None
    page = max(0, int(page))
    page_size = max(2, min(int(page_size), 32))
    selected = group["members"][page * page_size:(page + 1) * page_size]
    context = {group["parents"][item] for item in selected if group["parents"][item] and group["parents"][item] not in selected}
    ids = selected + sorted(context)
    if not ids:
        return {"id": group_id, "size": group["size"], "page": page, "page_size": page_size, "pages": (group["size"] + page_size - 1) // page_size, "nodes": [], "edges": [], "order_feedback": []}

import json

from . import query


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "map"

    def log_message(self, format, *args):
        """Avoid putting private search terms or entry IDs in access logs."""
        return

    def do_GET(self):
        if self.headers.get("Host", "").split(":", 1)[0] not in ("127.0.0.1", "localhost"):
            self.send_error(403)
            return
        parsed = urlparse(self.path)
        params = parse_qs(parsed.query)
        try:
            if parsed.path == "/api/map/groups":
                self.send_json(query.map_groups(params.get("offset", [0])[0], params.get("limit", [8])[0]))
            elif parsed.path == "/api/map/group":
                self.send_json(query.map_group(params.get("id", [""])[0][:100], params.get("page", [0])[0]))
            elif parsed.path == "/api/library/resources":
                self.send_json(query.library_resources())
            elif parsed.path == "/api/library/records":
                self.send_json(query.library_records(params.get("resource", ["node"])[0], params.get("page", [0])[0], search=params.get("q", [""])[0]))
            elif parsed.path == "/api/library/record":
                self.send_json(query.library_record(params.get("resource", ["node"])[0], params.get("id", [""])[0][:200]))
            elif parsed.path == "/api/search":
                self.send_json(query.search_entries(params.get("q", [""])[0][:200], 30))
            elif parsed.path == "/api/entry":
                self.send_json(query.get_entry(params.get("id", [""])[0][:100]))
            elif parsed.path == "/api/neighbors":
                self.send_json(query.neighbors(params.get("id", [""])[0][:100]))
            elif parsed.path in ("/", "/app.js", "/style.css"):
                name = "index.html" if parsed.path == "/" else parsed.path.lstrip("/")
                content_type = "text/html" if name.endswith(".html") else "text/javascript" if name.endswith(".js") else "text/css"
                body = (ROOT / name).read_bytes()
                self.send_response(200)
                self.send_header("Content-Type", content_type + "; charset=utf-8")
                self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
                self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-store")
                self.send_header("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")
                self.send_header("Content-Security-Policy", "default-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'")
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(body)
            else:
                self.send_error(404)
        except ValueError:
            self.send_json({"error": "Invalid query"}, 400)
        except Exception:
            self.send_json({"error": "Graph query failed"}, 500)

    def send_json(self, value, status=200):
        """Send UTF-8 JSON without allowing cached personal data."""
        body = json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False).encode()
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-store")
        self.send_header("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

from mgraph.cli import config,database,PROFILE_VERSION
from mgraph.profile_quality import build_passages,_supported_fact,quote_supported
schema=config()
with database() as conn:
    rows=conn.execute(f"SELECT e.id,e.label,e.evidence_text,p.profile,coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('kind',x.kind,'text',x.text_content,'observed_at',x.updated_at::text) ORDER BY x.kind) FILTER (WHERE x.kind IS NOT NULL),'[]'::jsonb) FROM {schema}.entry e JOIN {schema}.profile p ON p.entry_id=e.id AND p.prompt_version=%s AND p.model='kimi-k3' LEFT JOIN {schema}.extraction x ON x.entry_id=e.id AND NOT x.partial AND (left(x.kind,4)<>'web:' OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM {schema}.web_identity w JOIN {schema}.source_record n ON n.resource='node' AND n.id=substring(x.kind from 5) WHERE w.entry_id=x.entry_id AND w.kind=x.kind AND w.status='accepted' AND w.saved_hash=n.sha256 AND w.extraction_updated_at=x.updated_at)) GROUP BY e.id,p.profile ORDER BY e.id",(PROFILE_VERSION,)).fetchall()

    passages={p['passage_id']:p for p in build_passages(entry_id,source_text,extras)}
    for fact in profile.get('property_facts',[]):
        if _supported_fact(fact,passages): continue
        passage=passages.get(fact.get('passage_id'))
        reason='missing passage' if not passage else 'id mismatch' if fact.get('evidence_id')!=passage['evidence_id'] else 'unsupported quote'
        summary[(fact.get('key'),reason)]+=1
        if len(examples)<12: examples.append({'entry':entry_id,'key':fact.get('key'),'reason':reason,'quote_chars':len(fact.get('quote','')),'label_chars':len(label or ''),'quote_is_label':fact.get('quote')==label})

        passage=passages.get(claim.get('passage_id'))
        reason='missing passage' if not passage else 'id mismatch' if claim.get('evidence_id')!=passage['evidence_id'] else 'unsupported quote'
        summary[('claim',reason)]+=1
print('failure_kinds',summary)
print('examples',examples)

def anchor_saved_name(profile, entry_id, label, passages):
    """Make the saved entry title primary while retaining other names as cited facts."""
    if not isinstance(label, str) or not label.strip():
        return profile
    passage = next((item for item in passages if item["evidence_id"] == entry_id and item["origin"] == "source" and label in item["text"]), None)
    if passage is None:
        return profile
    start = passage["text"].find(label)
    quote_start = max(0, min(start, len(passage["text"]) - 8))
    quote_end = max(start + len(label), min(len(passage["text"]), quote_start + 8))
    anchor = {"key": "name", "value": label.strip(), "evidence_id": entry_id, "passage_id": passage["passage_id"], "quote": passage["text"][quote_start:quote_end], "kind": "observation", "confidence": "high", "observed_at": None, "origin": "source"}
    facts = [fact for fact in profile.get("property_facts", []) if not (fact.get("key") == "name" and fact.get("value") == anchor["value"] and fact.get("passage_id") == anchor["passage_id"]) ]
    profile["property_facts"] = [anchor] + facts
    profile["properties"] = properties_from_facts(profile["property_facts"])
    return profile


  wait "$worker_pid" || failed=1
done

from mgraph.cli import config,database,PROFILE_VERSION
from mgraph.profile_quality import build_passages,profile_issues,anchor_saved_name
schema=config()
with database() as conn:

issues=[]

    passages=build_passages(entry_id,source_text,extras)

```

`zsh run_parallel_profiles.sh` applies the pilot migration, screens fetched web identities, repairs saved primary names in completed profiles, runs four disjoint Kimi profile shards, audits every eligible current-version profile, then runs Cloudflare embeddings and up to 20,000 distinct Kimi pair judgments. The audit stops downstream inference if any eligible profile is missing, stale, or has unsupported quotes, or if a web page has not been screened. The script resumes from versioned persisted projections. Kimi K3 profiling and identity screening default to `low` reasoning effort; set `MGRAPH_DO_PROFILE_REASONING_EFFORT` or `MGRAPH_DO_IDENTITY_REASONING_EFFORT` in `.env` to evaluate another effort level. Pair judgments use the model default unless `MGRAPH_DO_REASONING_EFFORT` is set. Run `.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`, inspect `mgraph status`, and manually compare sampled claims and property quotes with `read_memory` before restarting a large run after a profile change.

Run the prototype with `uv run python -m mgraph.map_server` and open `http://127.0.0.1:8765`. The Proximity map loads connected group summaries eight at a time as the horizontal canvas scrolls; it never plots standalone entries. Each visible group loads 24 new entries per page, with bridge entries from earlier pages so every displayed entry remains connected. Offscreen group cards and edges are discarded. Persisted pair scores drive spring distances, pair feedback overrides model scores, and closer-than feedback adjusts positions when all three entries are on the same page. The grouping threshold is 0.65. Group topology is cached for 30 seconds, so newly judged pairs may take up to 30 seconds to appear. Search still covers every projected entry, including entries without a profile or graph position.

They are synthetic and too small to estimate production accuracy. The real-account comparison used saved Orca and Synara pages after public-page extraction and GLM-5.3 profiling.

| Model | Fixed labels | Ordering | Fixed-call time | Estimated fixed-call cost | Real Orca/Synara relation |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| GLM-5.3 | 3/4 | pass | 22.44 s | $0.004182 | `same_product`, 0.90 on the final profile format |
| Kimi K3 | 4/4 | pass | 41.86 s | $0.028485 | `same_niche`, 0.87 on the final profile format |

GLM called the synthetic ADE pair `same_product` instead of `same_niche`, though it ranked that pair closer than a general coding IDE. It also called the real saved Orca and Synara pages `same_product` in the final comparison. Kimi distinguished `same_niche` in both. On the final profile format, GLM took 10.49 seconds and approximately $0.00465, including cached input; Kimi took 17.4 seconds and approximately $0.01844. Output token counts and latency vary between requests; these figures are observations, not guarantees.

The pilot should use GLM-5.3 for entry profiling and Kimi K3 for pair judgments where the relation label drives graph placement. A cheaper first-pass judge could be introduced after a larger user-reviewed set with hard negatives, cross-medium conceptual echoes, and page-content hallucination checks establishes its recall and error rate. DigitalOcean's [serverless pricing](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/details/pricing/) lists GLM-5.3 at $1.40 per million input tokens and $4.40 per million output tokens, versus Kimi K3 at $3.00 and $15.00. Cached input is billed at lower rates and is recorded separately by the pipeline. After profiling the saved Cursor page, Kimi judged Cursor against both saved ADE pages at 0.62, below the Orca/Synara 0.87 judgment; this is a useful real-account sanity check, not a broad accuracy measure.

At 80 real GLM-5.3 profile calls, the observed average was 2,270 prompt tokens, 1,096 output tokens, and 24.7 seconds. The observed token shape is used for the whole-account estimate below, with cached input separated from uncached input. Long documents, skipped thin media, retries, and rate limits make any full-run forecast uncertain. The pipeline checkpoints every successful entry so larger runs can be resumed and measured in batches.

Three 27,000-31,000-character source entries exercised the long-profile path. Two were profiled with GLM-5.3 after segment splitting and evidence-ID normalization; one required a Kimi K3 profile after repeated malformed GLM JSON. The Kimi call took 241.7 seconds and used 23,916 prompt and 10,926 completion tokens. Current profiles are preserved on ordinary reruns even when a fallback model was used. This case illustrates why the naive whole-account cost and duration estimate does not cover the long tail.

## Whole-account inference sizing

The current snapshot has 5,017 projected entries. The profile gate admits 4,970 with enough available evidence, including 69 already profiled, leaving 4,901. Across 80 successful GLM-5.3 profile calls, mean usage was 2,270 input tokens, including 689 cached, and 1,096 output tokens. At [Kimi K3 pricing](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/details/pricing/) of $3 per million uncached input tokens, $0.30 cached input tokens, and $15 output tokens, applying that *GLM token shape* to Kimi gives $0.02139 per profile or about **$105 for the remaining 4,901**. Kimi's actual output length, failed calls, and long documents can materially change this; the one measured long Kimi profile cost about $0.22.

Across 54 logged Kimi K3 pair judgments, mean usage was 1,857 input tokens, including 90 cached, and 846 output tokens, for **$0.01801 per successful pair** at current rates. That implies about **$180 for 10,000** or **$360 for 20,000** judged pairs. The present 69-profile graph offers 468 candidate pairs at the current retrieval settings; projecting this density to 4,970 profiles yields roughly 34,000 candidate pairs and about **$607 in pair inference**, or **$712 for profiling plus pair inference** before failed calls, long tails, image processing, embeddings, storage, and any source expansion. Candidate density can change as the graph fills, so 34,000 is a sizing scenario rather than a fixed work count. A 10,000-20,000-pair budget gives a roughly $285-$465 successful-call baseline, with additional allowance needed for retries and unusually long entries.

The observed DigitalOcean model response headers showed 360 requests/minute, 3 million tokens/minute, a 180 million-token daily bucket, and about 18 million tokens remaining at the probe time. [Tier 4 publishes ceilings](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/details/limits/) of up to 360 requests/minute and 12 million tokens/minute; actual limits and available capacity can be lower. A single sequential worker has been far below the minute ceilings, while a full graph can consume more than the then-reported daily remainder. The pipeline now uses quota headers, bounded 429/503 retries, a 100,000-token daily reserve, and committed per-entry checkpoints. Run bounded batches, resume after quota recovery, and increase worker count only after observing headers. DigitalOcean [documents continuous quota refill and shared capacity](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/reference/quota-specific-response-headers/), so neither the Tier 4 number nor this snapshot guarantees zero throttling.

DigitalOcean [requires a positive prepaid balance for serverless inference](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/details/pricing/). Its [Startups terms](https://www.digitalocean.com/startups) distinguish DigitalOcean-hosted models from third-party passthrough models for core-credit eligibility, while [prepayment terms](https://www.digitalocean.com/legal/serverless_inference_prepayment) say restricted credits alone do not satisfy the prepayment gate. Confirm the actual award and account balance before a large run; the dollar estimates above are usage costs regardless of credit coverage.

## Other DigitalOcean model candidates

The additional `alternative-evaluation.json` run used the same four synthetic relation cases. It checks parser compatibility and a few distinctions, not production graph quality. Successful cases initially used a 1,100-token output cap; failures were rerun with a 3,500-token cap and, if needed, one 6,000-token retry, so the timing and cost columns are not a controlled head-to-head benchmark. Failed preliminary calls are not included in the listed successful-call costs.

| Model | Exact labels | Valid outputs | Ordering | Successful-call cost | Observation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
| Kimi K2.6 | 4/4 | 4/4 | pass | $0.01956 | Needs `temperature=1`; a repeated cross-medium case changed label between runs. |
| DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 | 3/4 | 4/4 | pass | $0.00354 | Fast; treated the cross-medium echo as `same_niche`. |
| MiMo V2.5 Pro | 3/4 | 4/4 | pass | $0.01379 | Valid with larger output budget; cross-medium label changed on repeat. |
| GLM-5.3 Flash | 3/4 | 4/4 | pass | $0.00042 | Called close ADEs `same_product`. |
| Nemotron 3 Ultra | 3/4 | 4/4 | pass | $0.00378 | Called the cross-medium echo `same_niche`. |
| Qwen 3.5 397B A17B | incomplete | incomplete | unmeasured | unmeasured | The 1,100-token budget produced no JSON; one larger-budget case succeeded, but the remaining run stalled and was stopped. |

All these model IDs are in the current [DigitalOcean catalog](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/details/models/), and their token rates are in [DigitalOcean pricing](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/details/pricing/). Kimi K2.6, DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813, and MiMo V2.5 Pro are the next useful comparisons on a reviewed sample of actual Memotron pairs. GLM-5.3 Flash is worth testing as a low-cost candidate generator. Kimi K3 remains the stronger measured judge for the saved Orca/Synara distinction, but four synthetic cases and a handful of real pairs are insufficient to choose a final model.

In a real cross-medium check, a saved Markdown entry and a web page received a Kimi `same_niche` judgment at 0.72. Two other vector-nearest candidates for long entries scored 0.05 and 0.08 after pair judgment. This supports using embeddings for recall and reasoning for the final relation; it does not establish graph-wide accuracy.

## Transcription economics

The source contains 69 audio nodes with 94.67 recorded minutes. Forty-five lacked a transcript, totaling 72.47 minutes.
