./README.md:37:`zsh run_parallel_profiles.sh` applies the pilot migration, screens fetched web identities, repairs saved primary names, refreshes stale Kimi judgments, and runs disjoint Kimi profile shards. It then repairs names again, audits every eligible current-version profile, runs disjoint Cloudflare embedding shards, refreshes judgments invalidated by new profiles, and runs disjoint Kimi relation shards up to 20,000 distinct pairs. Finally it persists clusters and neighbors, analyzes cited layout signals for multi-entry clusters in disjoint shards, rebuilds the graph, and annotates up to 40 clusters. Defaults are eight refresh, sixteen profile, four embedding, eight relation, and eight signal workers; `MGRAPH_REFRESH_WORKERS`, `MGRAPH_PROFILE_WORKERS`, `MGRAPH_EMBED_WORKERS`, `MGRAPH_RELATION_WORKERS`, and `MGRAPH_SIGNAL_WORKERS` set each stage independently. The audit stops downstream inference if any eligible profile is missing, stale, or has unsupported quotes, or if a web page has not been screened. The script resumes from versioned persisted projections. Kimi K3 profiling and identity screening default to `low` reasoning effort; set `MGRAPH_DO_PROFILE_REASONING_EFFORT` or `MGRAPH_DO_IDENTITY_REASONING_EFFORT` in `.env` to evaluate another effort level. Pair judgments use the model default unless `MGRAPH_DO_REASONING_EFFORT` is set. Run `.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`, inspect `mgraph status`, and manually compare sampled claims and property quotes with `read_memory` before restarting a large run after a profile change.
./README.md:39:Run the prototype with `uv run python -m mgraph.map_server` and open `http://127.0.0.1:8765`. The overview shows persisted multi-entry clusters in a two-dimensional graph, with solid judged links and dashed embedding suggestions. Select a cluster to show its first 24 memories in the center and all ranked neighboring clusters in previews on both sides; selecting a preview changes the focus. A group picker filters the overview by persisted topic group and can include singleton clusters. Generic layout signals select graph, timeline, sequence, place, gallery, or place-plus-timeline arrangements. Place layouts currently show cited place labels, not geographic coordinates; a true map needs coordinate resolution. Unknown dates or order remain unplaced. Search still covers every projected entry, including entries without a profile or graph position. #!/bin/zsh
set -u
cd /Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/agent/experiments/mgraph

worker_count=${MGRAPH_EMBED_WORKERS:-4}
if [[ ! "$worker_count" =~ '^[1-9][0-9]*$' ]]; then
  print "MGRAPH_EMBED_WORKERS must be a positive integer"
  exit 2
fi

while pgrep -f '[r]un_parallel_profiles.sh' >/dev/null && ! pgrep -f '[p]ython -m mgraph profile --model kimi-k3' >/dev/null; do
  sleep 10
done

while pgrep -f '[p]ython -m mgraph profile --model kimi-k3' >/dev/null; do
  print "m graph rolling embeddings: $worker_count disjoint shards"
  typeset -a worker_pids
  worker_pids=()
  for (( shard = 0; shard < worker_count; shard++ )); do
    uv run python -m mgraph embed --shard "$shard" --shards "$worker_count" &
    worker_pids+=("$!")
  done
  failed=0
  for worker_pid in "${worker_pids[@]}"; do
    wait "$worker_pid" || failed=1
  done
  if (( failed != 0 )); then
    print "m graph rolling embeddings paused; one or more shards failed"
    exit 1
  fi
  uv run python -m mgraph refresh-graph || exit 1
  sleep 300
done

print "m graph rolling embeddings complete; final embedding pass belongs to the backfill runner"

# m graph pilot

Local development lives here. The pilot reads one user's legacy Memotron data from DynamoDB, stores derived graph records in hosted PostgreSQL, and stores source snapshots and extraction artifacts in a private Cloudflare R2 bucket. The loopback-only cluster map and local MCP server consume the same projection.

## Pipeline

The source stage reads only the six Memotron partitions (`node`, `file`, `link`, `collection`, `property`, `linkTag`) for the configured user. Each DynamoDB query page becomes a compressed, hashed R2 object and is upserted into the dedicated PostgreSQL schema. Page checkpoints make interrupted runs resumable. The source partitions are not a transactional point-in-time snapshot. A later catch-up generation is needed to incorporate edits after this completed backfill.

The projection stage identifies top-level entries, treats the legacy `$NONE` reference sentinel as empty, resolves reciprocal page/clip references, and folds child blocks into cited evidence without shortening source blocks or dropping descendants. Public-page HTML, owned file media, profiles, embeddings, and pair judgments are separately versioned derivations. An entry's source hash and each derivation's source hash determine whether it needs recomputation. Raw fetched page and media bytes go to R2; PostgreSQL holds searchable text, structured profiles, a 1,024-dimensional pgvector projection, and relation judgments. Before profiling, a resumable web-identity screen compares each fetched page with the saved title, URL, and description. Obvious matches are accepted; title conflicts, private-page URLs, and login fallbacks receive a Kimi judgment. Conflicting or uncertain page text is quarantined from profiling, search, and MCP reads while the original saved record remains available. The screen deletes any affected derived profile, embedding, and pair judgments so they can be regenerated from accepted evidence. Profiling splits each source block and accepted extraction into overlapping passages of at most 2,800 characters, packs complete passages into model requests, and reconciles long-entry summaries and uncertainty. Claims and property facts carry an entry ID, passage ID, and exact supporting quote; a validator removes facts whose quote does not occur in that passage. The saved title is the single primary `name`; other cited names remain in property facts. Property facts retain confidence and extraction observation time, and common property aliases are normalized for comparison. Entries needing more than 64 model requests raise a visible error. The legacy vector DataFn schema is unused.

Candidate relations are the union of vector neighbors, lexical matches, explicit links, and shared extracted concepts. DO reasoning judges candidates and persists a 0-1 proximity score, relation type, explanation, and supporting entry IDs. The evidence profile captures concepts, tags, properties, claims, and uncertainty for later chat and comparison surfaces. Thin title-only records remain marked `thin` and should not be treated as fully understood.

The cluster stage persists every profiled entry in a stable cluster identity. Strong judged links at or above 0.80 form current components; judged cross-cluster links at or above 0.65 remain separate neighbor edges. Embedding centroids provide explicitly labeled suggestions when no judged link is available. The projection retains cluster identities by member overlap across rebuilds and stores membership, multiple neighbors, topic groups, and generic arrangement metadata. Groups are many-to-many domain proposals, not merged clusters. Profile domains are normalized before grouping, and very broad domains are excluded. Signals are a separately versioned derivation: deterministic cited profile facts, dated or numbered saved-note titles, and media types are merged with cited layout facts extracted from selected source passages for members of formed clusters. A note title's date is marked as a record date; publication dates do not count as event dates. This stage does not invalidate a saved profile or embedding. Cluster summaries are optional model annotations with source hashes; a changed member profile clears the annotation for review. Candidate pair retrieval routes through nearest persisted cluster centroids as an additional source while retaining global vector, lexical, concept, and explicit-link discovery.

## Run

Use Python 3.10 or newer. Run `uv sync --python python3.10` to install dependencies. No source snapshots or media are written to local disk.

```sh
uv run python -m mgraph migrate
uv run python -m mgraph backfill
uv run python -m mgraph project
uv run python -m mgraph enrich-web --limit 20
uv run python -m mgraph enrich-audio --limit 1
uv run python -m mgraph enrich-image --limit 1
uv run python -m mgraph enrich-pdf --limit 1
uv run python -m mgraph profile --limit 10 --model kimi-k3
uv run python -m mgraph embed --limit 10
uv run python -m mgraph relate --limit 5 --model kimi-k3
uv run python -m mgraph refresh-graph
uv run python -m mgraph enrich-signals --model kimi-k3 --limit 5
uv run python -m mgraph refresh-graph
uv run python -m mgraph annotate-clusters --model kimi-k3 --limit 5
uv run python -m mgraph status
```

`zsh run_parallel_profiles.sh` applies the pilot migration, screens fetched web identities, repairs saved primary names, refreshes stale Kimi judgments, and runs disjoint Kimi profile shards. It then repairs names again, audits every eligible current-version profile, runs disjoint Cloudflare embedding shards, refreshes judgments invalidated by new profiles, and runs disjoint Kimi relation shards up to 20,000 distinct pairs. Finally it persists clusters and neighbors, analyzes cited layout signals for multi-entry clusters in disjoint shards, rebuilds the graph, and annotates up to 40 clusters. Defaults are eight refresh, sixteen profile, four embedding, eight relation, and eight signal workers; `MGRAPH_REFRESH_WORKERS`, `MGRAPH_PROFILE_WORKERS`, `MGRAPH_EMBED_WORKERS`, `MGRAPH_RELATION_WORKERS`, and `MGRAPH_SIGNAL_WORKERS` set each stage independently. The audit stops downstream inference if any eligible profile is missing, stale, or has unsupported quotes, or if a web page has not been screened. The script resumes from versioned persisted projections. Kimi K3 profiling and identity screening default to `low` reasoning effort; set `MGRAPH_DO_PROFILE_REASONING_EFFORT` or `MGRAPH_DO_IDENTITY_REASONING_EFFORT` in `.env` to evaluate another effort level. Pair judgments use the model default unless `MGRAPH_DO_REASONING_EFFORT` is set. Run `.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`, inspect `mgraph status`, and manually compare sampled claims and property quotes with `read_memory` before restarting a large run after a profile change.

Run the prototype with `uv run python -m mgraph.map_server` and open `http://127.0.0.1:8765`. The overview shows persisted multi-entry clusters in a two-dimensional graph, with solid judged links and dashed embedding suggestions. Select a cluster to show its first 24 memories in the center and all ranked neighboring clusters in previews on both sides; selecting a preview changes the focus. A group picker filters the overview by persisted topic group and can include singleton clusters. Generic layout signals select graph, timeline, sequence, place, gallery, or place-plus-timeline arrangements. Place layouts currently show cited place labels, not geographic coordinates; a true map needs coordinate resolution. Unknown dates or order remain unplaced. Search still covers every projected entry, including entries without a profile or graph position. The saved graph updates through `refresh-graph`; rolling embeddings refresh it during a live backfill.

The Library tab pages authoritative DynamoDB source records by `node`, `file`, `link`, `collection`, `property`, and `linkTag`. On `node`, the `Profiled entries only` filter limits search, counts, and pagination to source records with a saved profile. Record details show raw source fields, associated root entry evidence, extraction output, profile concepts/tags/properties/claims, and embedding and pair-judgment status when available. The entry API also returns each extraction's identity status and reason; the Library continues to expose raw quarantined text for inspection, while MCP reads omit it. The library reads hosted PostgreSQL and does not download R2 snapshots or rerun inference. For a manual check, open the library, filter to profiled entries, search and advance a filtered page, inspect a profile, switch resources, then return to the map and open a multi-entry cluster. Verify that judged and suggested neighbors are labeled distinctly, select a neighbor preview, and use the group picker to browse a topic. The map is a pilot visualization, and overview coordinates are recalculated for the displayed set rather than being stable global coordinates.

The local MCP server runs over stdio with `/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/agent/experiments/mgraph/.venv/bin/python -m mgraph.mcp_server`. Use that absolute executable path and `-m mgraph.mcp_server` as arguments in an AI host's MCP configuration; no special working directory is needed. It exposes read-only `search_memories`, `read_memory`, `nearby_memories`, `compare_memories`, and `tabulate_memory_differences` tools. The last tool assembles persisted properties and cited claims side by side so an agent can answer comparisons without refetching source pages. Both in-process and subprocess MCP client calls passed. A connected agent can read the private one-user memory projection returned by these tools.

For hosts that accept the common JSON stdio shape:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "memotron-mgraph": {
      "command": "/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/agent/experiments/mgraph/.venv/bin/python",
      "args": ["-m", "mgraph.mcp_server"]
    }
  }
}
```

`--entry node:<id>` selects specific entries for enrichment, profiling, and embedding. `relate --left node:<id> --right node:<id>` judges a specific pair. Public page extraction can be partitioned with `--shard 0 --shards 4` through shard 3. Successful derivations are skipped on rerun; `enrich-web --refresh` fetches already processed pages again. An omitted `--limit` processes every eligible item and may entail substantial external API usage.

`zsh run_full.sh` runs the remaining public-page retry, Kimi K3 vision and profile derivation, Cloudflare embedding, and a first pass capped at 20,000 distinct Kimi-judged pairs across all restarts. Rerun the same script after a provider pause or process interruption: completed per-item derivations are skipped, and changed vision models invalidate prior image and scanned-PDF extraction hashes. The script reads the fixed DynamoDB snapshot already held in PostgreSQL and R2; it does not include later source edits.

After extraction, `zsh run_parallel_profiles.sh` screens page identity, refreshes stale judgments, runs disjoint Kimi profile shards, audits them, then embeds and judges pairs in disjoint shards. Relation budgets are computed from saved per-shard pair counts, keeping the 20,000-pair cap across restarts. Do not run it alongside `run_full.sh` or another profiling worker. It is safe to restart after interruption because screened pages, current profiles, embeddings, and current judgments are skipped. If screening or any shard exits unsuccessfully, the script stops before advancing to the next stage so the failed stage can be resumed deliberately.

During profiling, `zsh run_rolling_embeddings.sh` refreshes new embeddings in four disjoint Cloudflare shards, then rebuilds the saved cluster graph and waits five minutes. It exits when the profile workers stop; the backfill runner performs a final embedding and graph pass after its profile audit. This makes newly profiled entries available to the map while the long profile stage continues.

Profiling normally preserves a current profile even if a long entry required another model. Passing `profile --model <name>` explicitly recomputes profiles made by a different model; this is useful for model comparisons and can incur substantial inference cost.

DigitalOcean calls are sequential within each CLI worker. On HTTP 429 or 503, the client uses `Retry-After` and quota reset headers for bounded retries. If the indicated wait exceeds two minutes or repeated attempts fail, the command stops with `InferencePaused`; completed entries remain committed and a later rerun resumes them. Profile and relation inference release database reads before calling the model and retry atomic result/usage writes after a database restart without rerunning the model when the result was already committed. The client also checks the daily tokens remaining in successful response headers before the next request and pauses at `MGRAPH_DO_DAILY_RESERVE_TOKENS` (default 100,000), allowing for estimated prompt and completion tokens. This is a best-effort per-process guard because other account workloads and workers can consume the same allowance. Check live model-specific headers and observe 429s when changing worker counts. DigitalOcean's published Tier 4 ceiling is higher than the model-specific limits actually returned by the API.

`neighbors --entry node:<id>` returns the currently judged proximity order. User corrections can be recorded with `feedback-pair --left ... --right ... --score 0.9 --label same_niche` and `feedback-order --anchor ... --closer ... --farther ...`. Feedback is stored separately from model judgments and applied when returning neighbors. For a page that requires the authenticated Aside browser, pipe its extracted text into `import-text --entry node:<id> --source-node node:<id>`; this puts the text in R2 and the projection without making a local data file.

`python3 -m mgraph evaluate` runs four fixed synthetic relation cases against GLM-5.3 and Kimi K3 and writes `evaluation.json`. This checks JSON validity, evidence IDs, proximity ordering, latency, and token cost. It is a smoke test, not a labeled corpus evaluation. A user-reviewed test set from actual Memotron entries is still needed before treating the scores as accuracy measurements.

`python3 -m mgraph.evaluate_alternatives` runs the same synthetic cases against other DigitalOcean-hosted models and writes `alternative-evaluation.json`. Valid previous results are retained on rerun, so malformed outputs can be retried with a larger output budget without repeating successful calls. The comparison and whole-account cost scenarios are in `EVALUATION.md`.

The media extractor reads only S3 URLs in the configured user's legacy `tidyfiles` bucket. DynamoDB uses `MGRAPH_SOURCE_AWS_PROFILE`; file reads use `MGRAPH_SOURCE_S3_AWS_PROFILE`, which defaults to the DynamoDB profile. The available `data` profile passed a one-byte object read and is configured for this pilot. The extractor prefers an optional OpenAI-compatible Whisper endpoint on a DigitalOcean GPU Droplet when `MGRAPH_DO_TRANSCRIPTION_URL` is set; otherwise it uses Cloudflare Workers AI Whisper Large V3 Turbo with voice activity filtering. Large audio files are decoded with FFmpeg in memory and transcribed in four-minute chunks; this path requires `ffmpeg` on `PATH`. The DO serverless model catalog currently has no dedicated transcription endpoint. Image-only PDFs fall back to in-memory page rendering and DigitalOcean vision OCR for documents up to 20 pages. Existing transcripts and source metadata are also indexed.

Extraction has visible bounds: 260,000 characters for an HTML page, 100 pages and 260,000 characters for selectable PDF text, 20 pages for scanned PDF OCR, 80 MB for audio, and 30 MB for each PDF or image. Large raster images and GIF first frames are resized in memory before vision inference. Oversized sources keep their metadata in the R2 DynamoDB snapshot and their original bytes in legacy S3; each gets an `extraction_failure` row. Two earlier 80,000-character extracts that were found to be incomplete are marked `partial` and excluded from profiling and rich-evidence counts. Three saved PDFs are 262, 274, and 613 pages; they need a separate book-scale chapter projection before their full text can be profiled without losing coverage. Voice activity filtering can return no words on very short or non-speech audio, which is recorded as an empty-extraction failure.

## Pilot validation

The September 27, 2026 source backfill stored 37,917 records across 80 R2 pages; PostgreSQL record count and page row totals match. The root resolver handles the legacy `$NONE` sentinel, reciprocal page/clip references, and missing parent nodes; the corrected projection contains 5,017 top-level entries. R2 page 20 passed a decompression and SHA-256 check. A source audit found four formerly shortened blocks across three entries; all three were reprojected with full source text and profiled. Public-page extraction covered 2,302 of 2,551 web nodes. Media extraction recorded 235 image, 24 audio, and 26 PDF results; one web and one PDF result are marked partial and excluded from profiles. There are 250 web, 11 image, 21 audio, and 5 PDF failure rows, including records that overlap those partial results. The `data` AWS profile read legacy file objects, and saved audio, image, and PDF passed the complete S3-to-R2 extraction path. The inference sample has 69 profiles, 69 embeddings, and 53 judged relations, all current against their profile evidence. A full map of all 5,017 entries still requires a larger inference run. In one cross-medium sample, a saved Markdown entry and a web page received a `same_niche` relation at 0.72, while two high-vector-similarity pairs were judged 0.05 and 0.08; this is a concrete check of the candidate-and-judge split, not an accuracy benchmark.

## Configuration

Fill the remaining blanks in the ignored `.env` in this directory. `.env.example` documents every setting. Do not put credentials in the example file.

- `MGRAPH_DATABASE_URL`: a hosted PostgreSQL connection string with TLS. Use a dedicated database or schema; the provider must support `pgvector`.
- `MGRAPH_DO_MODEL_ACCESS_KEY`: a DigitalOcean serverless inference model access key. The listed reasoning and vision models are starting choices to benchmark.
- `MGRAPH_DO_PROFILE_REASONING_EFFORT` and `MGRAPH_DO_IDENTITY_REASONING_EFFORT`: reasoning effort for Kimi profile extraction and selective web identity judgments; both default to `low` in the pilot. `MGRAPH_DO_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` bounds each model request.
- `MGRAPH_DO_PROFILE_MODEL`, `MGRAPH_DO_RELATION_MODEL`, and `MGRAPH_DO_VISION_MODEL`: select Kimi K3 for profiles, pair judgments, and image understanding in the full pilot. The earlier GLM and Nemotron results remain in the evaluation history.
- `MGRAPH_CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `MGRAPH_CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_AI_API_TOKEN`: Workers AI REST access for embeddings and transcription.
- `MGRAPH_R2_BUCKET`, `MGRAPH_R2_ENDPOINT`, `MGRAPH_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, and `MGRAPH_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`: a private bucket and bucket-scoped S3 API credentials with object read/write access. R2 credentials are distinct from the Workers AI token.
- `MGRAPH_SOURCE_AWS_PROFILE`, `MGRAPH_SOURCE_S3_AWS_PROFILE`, `MGRAPH_SOURCE_AWS_REGION`, `MGRAPH_SOURCE_DYNAMODB_TABLE`, and `MGRAPH_SOURCE_USER_ID`: identify the read-only source and its separate file-read identity.

# m graph pilot

Local development lives here. The pilot reads one user's legacy Memotron data from DynamoDB, stores derived graph records in hosted PostgreSQL, and stores source snapshots and extraction artifacts in a private Cloudflare R2 bucket. The loopback-only cluster map and local MCP server consume the same projection.

## Pipeline

The source stage reads only the six Memotron partitions (`node`, `file`, `link`, `collection`, `property`, `linkTag`) for the configured user. Each DynamoDB query page becomes a compressed, hashed R2 object and is upserted into the dedicated PostgreSQL schema. Page checkpoints make interrupted runs resumable. The source partitions are not a transactional point-in-time snapshot. A later catch-up generation is needed to incorporate edits after this completed backfill.

The projection stage identifies top-level entries, treats the legacy `$NONE` reference sentinel as empty, resolves reciprocal page/clip references, and folds child blocks into cited evidence without shortening source blocks or dropping descendants. Public-page HTML, owned file media, profiles, embeddings, and pair judgments are separately versioned derivations. An entry's source hash and each derivation's source hash determine whether it needs recomputation. Raw fetched page and media bytes go to R2; PostgreSQL holds searchable text, structured profiles, a 1,024-dimensional pgvector projection, and relation judgments. Before profiling, a resumable web-identity screen compares each fetched page with the saved title, URL, and description. Obvious matches are accepted; title conflicts, private-page URLs, and login fallbacks receive a Kimi judgment. Conflicting or uncertain page text is quarantined from profiling, search, and MCP reads while the original saved record remains available. The screen deletes any affected derived profile, embedding, and pair judgments so they can be regenerated from accepted evidence. Profiling splits each source block and accepted extraction into overlapping passages of at most 2,800 characters, packs complete passages into model requests, and reconciles long-entry summaries and uncertainty. Claims and property facts carry an entry ID, passage ID, and exact supporting quote; a validator removes facts whose quote does not occur in that passage. The saved title is the single primary `name`; other cited names remain in property facts. Property facts retain confidence and extraction observation time, and common property aliases are normalized for comparison. Entries needing more than 64 model requests raise a visible error. The legacy vector DataFn schema is unused.

Candidate relations are the union of vector neighbors, lexical matches, explicit links, and shared extracted concepts. DO reasoning judges candidates and persists a 0-1 proximity score, relation type, explanation, and supporting entry IDs. The evidence profile captures concepts, tags, properties, claims, and uncertainty for later chat and comparison surfaces. Thin title-only records remain marked `thin` and should not be treated as fully understood.

The cluster stage persists every profiled entry in a stable cluster identity. Strong judged links at or above 0.80 form current components; judged cross-cluster links at or above 0.65 remain separate neighbor edges. Embedding centroids provide explicitly labeled suggestions when no judged link is available. The projection retains cluster identities by member overlap across rebuilds and stores membership, multiple neighbors, topic groups, and generic arrangement metadata. Groups are many-to-many domain proposals, not merged clusters. Profile domains are normalized before grouping, and very broad domains are excluded. Signals are a separately versioned derivation: deterministic cited profile facts, dated or numbered saved-note titles, and media types are merged with cited layout facts extracted from selected source passages for members of formed clusters. A note title's date is marked as a record date; publication dates do not count as event dates. This stage does not invalidate a saved profile or embedding. Cluster summaries are optional model annotations with source hashes; a changed member profile clears the annotation for review. Candidate pair retrieval routes through nearest persisted cluster centroids as an additional source while retaining global vector, lexical, concept, and explicit-link discovery.

## Run

Use Python 3.10 or newer. Run `uv sync --python python3.10` to install dependencies. No source snapshots or media are written to local disk.

```sh
uv run python -m mgraph backfill
uv run python -m mgraph project
uv run python -m mgraph enrich-web --limit 20
uv run python -m mgraph enrich-audio --limit 1
uv run python -m mgraph enrich-image --limit 1
uv run python -m mgraph enrich-pdf --limit 1
uv run python -m mgraph profile --limit 10 --model kimi-k3
uv run python -m mgraph embed --limit 10
uv run python -m mgraph relate --limit 5 --model kimi-k3
uv run python -m mgraph refresh-graph
uv run python -m mgraph enrich-signals --model kimi-k3 --limit 5
uv run python -m mgraph refresh-graph
uv run python -m mgraph annotate-clusters --model kimi-k3 --limit 5
uv run python -m mgraph status
```

`zsh run_parallel_profiles.sh` applies the pilot migration, screens fetched web identities, repairs saved primary names, refreshes stale Kimi judgments, and runs disjoint Kimi profile shards. It then repairs names again, audits every eligible current-version profile, runs disjoint Cloudflare embedding shards, refreshes judgments invalidated by new profiles, and runs disjoint Kimi relation shards up to 20,000 distinct pairs. Finally it persists clusters and neighbors, analyzes cited layout signals for multi-entry clusters in disjoint shards, rebuilds the graph, and annotates up to 40 clusters. Defaults are eight refresh, sixteen profile, four embedding, eight relation, and eight signal workers; `MGRAPH_REFRESH_WORKERS`, `MGRAPH_PROFILE_WORKERS`, `MGRAPH_EMBED_WORKERS`, `MGRAPH_RELATION_WORKERS`, and `MGRAPH_SIGNAL_WORKERS` set each stage independently. The audit stops downstream inference if any eligible profile is missing, stale, or has unsupported quotes, or if a web page has not been screened. The script resumes from versioned persisted projections. Kimi K3 profiling and identity screening default to `low` reasoning effort; set `MGRAPH_DO_PROFILE_REASONING_EFFORT` or `MGRAPH_DO_IDENTITY_REASONING_EFFORT` in `.env` to evaluate another effort level. Pair judgments use the model default unless `MGRAPH_DO_REASONING_EFFORT` is set. Run `.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`, inspect `mgraph status`, and manually compare sampled claims and property quotes with `read_memory` before restarting a large run after a profile change.

Run the prototype with `uv run python -m mgraph.map_server` and open `http://127.0.0.1:8765`. The overview shows persisted multi-entry clusters in a two-dimensional graph, with solid judged links and dashed embedding suggestions. Select a cluster to show its first 24 memories in the center and all ranked neighboring clusters in previews on both sides; selecting a preview changes the focus. A group picker filters the overview by persisted topic group and can include singleton clusters. Generic layout signals select graph, timeline, sequence, place, gallery, or place-plus-timeline arrangements. Place layouts currently show cited place labels, not geographic coordinates; a true map needs coordinate resolution. Unknown dates or order remain unplaced. Search still covers every projected entry, including entries without a profile or graph position. The saved graph updates through `refresh-graph`; rolling embeddings refresh it during a live backfill.

The Library tab pages authoritative DynamoDB source records by `node`, `file`, `link`, `collection`, `property`, and `linkTag`. On `node`, the `Profiled entries only` filter limits search, counts, and pagination to source records with a saved profile. Record details show raw source fields, associated root entry evidence, extraction output, profile concepts/tags/properties/claims, and embedding and pair-judgment status when available. The entry API also returns each extraction's identity status and reason; the Library continues to expose raw quarantined text for inspection, while MCP reads omit it. The library reads hosted PostgreSQL and does not download R2 snapshots or rerun inference. For a manual check, open the library, filter to profiled entries, search and advance a filtered page, inspect a profile, switch resources, then return to the map and open a multi-entry cluster. Verify that judged and suggested neighbors are labeled distinctly, select a neighbor preview, and use the group picker to browse a topic. The map is a pilot visualization, and overview coordinates are recalculated for the displayed set rather than being stable global coordinates.

The local MCP server runs over stdio with `/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/agent/experiments/mgraph/.venv/bin/python -m mgraph.mcp_server`. Use that absolute executable path and `-m mgraph.mcp_server` as arguments in an AI host's MCP configuration; no special working directory is needed. It exposes read-only `search_memories`, `read_memory`, `nearby_memories`, `compare_memories`, and `tabulate_memory_differences` tools. The last tool assembles persisted properties and cited claims side by side so an agent can answer comparisons without refetching source pages. Both in-process and subprocess MCP client calls passed. A connected agent can read the private one-user memory projection returned by these tools.

`--entry node:<id>` selects specific entries for enrichment, profiling, and embedding. `relate --left node:<id> --right node:<id>` judges a specific pair. Public page extraction can be partitioned with `--shard 0 --shards 4` through shard 3. Successful derivations are skipped on rerun; `enrich-web --refresh` fetches already processed pages again. An omitted `--limit` processes every eligible item and may entail substantial external API usage.

`zsh run_full.sh` runs the remaining public-page retry, Kimi K3 vision and profile derivation, Cloudflare embedding, and a first pass capped at 20,000 distinct Kimi-judged pairs across all restarts. Rerun the same script after a provider pause or process interruption: completed per-item derivations are skipped, and changed vision models invalidate prior image and scanned-PDF extraction hashes. The script reads the fixed DynamoDB snapshot already held in PostgreSQL and R2; it does not include later source edits.

After extraction, `zsh run_parallel_profiles.sh` screens page identity, refreshes stale judgments, runs disjoint Kimi profile shards, audits them, then embeds and judges pairs in disjoint shards. Relation budgets are computed from saved per-shard pair counts, keeping the 20,000-pair cap across restarts. Do not run it alongside `run_full.sh` or another profiling worker. It is safe to restart after interruption because screened pages, current profiles, embeddings, and current judgments are skipped. If screening or any shard exits unsuccessfully, the script stops before advancing to the next stage so the failed stage can be resumed deliberately.

During profiling, `zsh run_rolling_embeddings.sh` refreshes new embeddings in four disjoint Cloudflare shards, then rebuilds the saved cluster graph and waits five minutes. It exits when the profile workers stop; the backfill runner performs a final embedding and graph pass after its profile audit. This makes newly profiled entries available to the map while the long profile stage continues.

Profiling normally preserves a current profile even if a long entry required another model. Passing `profile --model <name>` explicitly recomputes profiles made by a different model; this is useful for model comparisons and can incur substantial inference cost.

DigitalOcean calls are sequential within each CLI worker. On HTTP 429 or 503, the client uses `Retry-After` and quota reset headers for bounded retries. If the indicated wait exceeds two minutes or repeated attempts fail, the command stops with `InferencePaused`; completed entries remain committed and a later rerun resumes them. Profile and relation inference release database reads before calling the model and retry atomic result/usage writes after a database restart without rerunning the model when the result was already committed. The client also checks the daily tokens remaining in successful response headers before the next request and pauses at `MGRAPH_DO_DAILY_RESERVE_TOKENS` (default 100,000), allowing for estimated prompt and completion tokens. This is a best-effort per-process guard because other account workloads and workers can consume the same allowance. Check live model-specific headers and observe 429s when changing worker counts. DigitalOcean's published Tier 4 ceiling is higher than the model-specific limits actually returned by the API.

`neighbors --entry node:<id>` returns the currently judged proximity order. User corrections can be recorded with `feedback-pair --left ... --right ... --score 0.9 --label same_niche` and `feedback-order --anchor ... --closer ... --farther ...`. Feedback is stored separately from model judgments and applied when returning neighbors. For a page that requires the authenticated Aside browser, pipe its extracted text into `import-text --entry node:<id> --source-node node:<id>`; this puts the text in R2 and the projection without making a local data file.

`python3 -m mgraph evaluate` runs four fixed synthetic relation cases against GLM-5.3 and Kimi K3 and writes `evaluation.json`. This checks JSON validity, evidence IDs, proximity ordering, latency, and token cost. It is a smoke test, not a labeled corpus evaluation. A user-reviewed test set from actual Memotron entries is still needed before treating the scores as accuracy measurements.

`python3 -m mgraph.evaluate_alternatives` runs the same synthetic cases against other DigitalOcean-hosted models and writes `alternative-evaluation.json`. Valid previous results are retained on rerun, so malformed outputs can be retried with a larger output budget without repeating successful calls. The comparison and whole-account cost scenarios are in `EVALUATION.md`.

The media extractor reads only S3 URLs in the configured user's legacy `tidyfiles` bucket. DynamoDB uses `MGRAPH_SOURCE_AWS_PROFILE`; file reads use `MGRAPH_SOURCE_S3_AWS_PROFILE`, which defaults to the DynamoDB profile. The available `data` profile passed a one-byte object read and is configured for this pilot. The extractor prefers an optional OpenAI-compatible Whisper endpoint on a DigitalOcean GPU Droplet when `MGRAPH_DO_TRANSCRIPTION_URL` is set; otherwise it uses Cloudflare Workers AI Whisper Large V3 Turbo with voice activity filtering. Large audio files are decoded with FFmpeg in memory and transcribed in four-minute chunks; this path requires `ffmpeg` on `PATH`. The DO serverless model catalog currently has no dedicated transcription endpoint. Image-only PDFs fall back to in-memory page rendering and DigitalOcean vision OCR for documents up to 20 pages. Existing transcripts and source metadata are also indexed.

Extraction has visible bounds: 260,000 characters for an HTML page, 100 pages and 260,000 characters for selectable PDF text, 20 pages for scanned PDF OCR, 80 MB for audio, and 30 MB for each PDF or image. Large raster images and GIF first frames are resized in memory before vision inference. Oversized sources keep their metadata in the R2 DynamoDB snapshot and their original bytes in legacy S3; each gets an `extraction_failure` row. Two earlier 80,000-character extracts that were found to be incomplete are marked `partial` and excluded from profiling and rich-evidence counts. Three saved PDFs are 262, 274, and 613 pages; they need a separate book-scale chapter projection before their full text can be profiled without losing coverage. Voice activity filtering can return no words on very short or non-speech audio, which is recorded as an empty-extraction failure.

## Pilot validation

The September 27, 2026 source backfill stored 37,917 records across 80 R2 pages; PostgreSQL record count and page row totals match. The root resolver handles the legacy `$NONE` sentinel, reciprocal page/clip references, and missing parent nodes; the corrected projection contains 5,017 top-level entries. R2 page 20 passed a decompression and SHA-256 check. A source audit found four formerly shortened blocks across three entries; all three were reprojected with full source text and profiled. Public-page extraction covered 2,302 of 2,551 web nodes. Media extraction recorded 235 image, 24 audio, and 26 PDF results; one web and one PDF result are marked partial and excluded from profiles. There are 250 web, 11 image, 21 audio, and 5 PDF failure rows, including records that overlap those partial results. The `data` AWS profile read legacy file objects, and saved audio, image, and PDF passed the complete S3-to-R2 extraction path. The inference sample has 69 profiles, 69 embeddings, and 53 judged relations, all current against their profile evidence. A full map of all 5,017 entries still requires a larger inference run. In one cross-medium sample, a saved Markdown entry and a web page received a `same_niche` relation at 0.72, while two high-vector-similarity pairs were judged 0.05 and 0.08; this is a concrete check of the candidate-and-judge split, not an accuracy benchmark.

## Configuration

Fill the remaining blanks in the ignored `.env` in this directory. `.env.example` documents every setting. Do not put credentials in the example file.

- `MGRAPH_DATABASE_URL`: a hosted PostgreSQL connection string with TLS. Use a dedicated database or schema; the provider must support `pgvector`.
- `MGRAPH_DO_MODEL_ACCESS_KEY`: a DigitalOcean serverless inference model access key. The listed reasoning and vision models are starting choices to benchmark.
- `MGRAPH_DO_PROFILE_REASONING_EFFORT` and `MGRAPH_DO_IDENTITY_REASONING_EFFORT`: reasoning effort for Kimi profile extraction and selective web identity judgments; both default to `low` in the pilot. `MGRAPH_DO_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` bounds each model request.
- `MGRAPH_DO_PROFILE_MODEL`, `MGRAPH_DO_RELATION_MODEL`, and `MGRAPH_DO_VISION_MODEL`: select Kimi K3 for profiles, pair judgments, and image understanding in the full pilot. The earlier GLM and Nemotron results remain in the evaluation history.
- `MGRAPH_CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `MGRAPH_CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_AI_API_TOKEN`: Workers AI REST access for embeddings and transcription.
- `MGRAPH_R2_BUCKET`, `MGRAPH_R2_ENDPOINT`, `MGRAPH_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, and `MGRAPH_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`: a private bucket and bucket-scoped S3 API credentials with object read/write access. R2 credentials are distinct from the Workers AI token.
- `MGRAPH_SOURCE_AWS_PROFILE`, `MGRAPH_SOURCE_S3_AWS_PROFILE`, `MGRAPH_SOURCE_AWS_REGION`, `MGRAPH_SOURCE_DYNAMODB_TABLE`, and `MGRAPH_SOURCE_USER_ID`: identify the read-only source and its separate file-read identity.

For the standard R2 jurisdiction, the endpoint is `https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`. A jurisdictional bucket needs its matching endpoint. Keep the bucket private. The backfill will use account-scoped object keys beneath `MGRAPH_R2_PREFIX` and keep object hashes and job checkpoints in PostgreSQL.

# m graph pilot

Local development lives here. The pilot reads one user's legacy Memotron data from DynamoDB, stores derived graph records in hosted PostgreSQL, and stores source snapshots and extraction artifacts in a private Cloudflare R2 bucket. The loopback-only cluster map and local MCP server consume the same projection.

## Pipeline

The source stage reads only the six Memotron partitions (`node`, `file`, `link`, `collection`, `property`, `linkTag`) for the configured user. Each DynamoDB query page becomes a compressed, hashed R2 object and is upserted into the dedicated PostgreSQL schema. Page checkpoints make interrupted runs resumable. The source partitions are not a transactional point-in-time snapshot. A later catch-up generation is needed to incorporate edits after this completed backfill.

The projection stage identifies top-level entries, treats the legacy `$NONE` reference sentinel as empty, resolves reciprocal page/clip references, and folds child blocks into cited evidence without shortening source blocks or dropping descendants. Public-page HTML, owned file media, profiles, embeddings, and pair judgments are separately versioned derivations. An entry's source hash and each derivation's source hash determine whether it needs recomputation. Raw fetched page and media bytes go to R2; PostgreSQL holds searchable text, structured profiles, a 1,024-dimensional pgvector projection, and relation judgments. Before profiling, a resumable web-identity screen compares each fetched page with the saved title, URL, and description. Obvious matches are accepted; title conflicts, private-page URLs, and login fallbacks receive a Kimi judgment. Conflicting or uncertain page text is quarantined from profiling, search, and MCP reads while the original saved record remains available. The screen deletes any affected derived profile, embedding, and pair judgments so they can be regenerated from accepted evidence. Profiling splits each source block and accepted extraction into overlapping passages of at most 2,800 characters, packs complete passages into model requests, and reconciles long-entry summaries and uncertainty. Claims and property facts carry an entry ID, passage ID, and exact supporting quote; a validator removes facts whose quote does not occur in that passage. The saved title is the single primary `name`; other cited names remain in property facts. Property facts retain confidence and extraction observation time, and common property aliases are normalized for comparison. Entries needing more than 64 model requests raise a visible error. The legacy vector DataFn schema is unused.

Candidate relations are the union of vector neighbors, lexical matches, explicit links, and shared extracted concepts. DO reasoning judges candidates and persists a 0-1 proximity score, relation type, explanation, and supporting entry IDs. The evidence profile captures concepts, tags, properties, claims, and uncertainty for later chat and comparison surfaces. Thin title-only records remain marked `thin` and should not be treated as fully understood.

The cluster stage persists every profiled entry in a stable cluster identity. Strong judged links at or above 0.80 form current components; judged cross-cluster links at or above 0.65 remain separate neighbor edges. Embedding centroids provide explicitly labeled suggestions when no judged link is available. The projection retains cluster identities by member overlap across rebuilds and stores membership, multiple neighbors, topic groups, and generic arrangement metadata. Groups are many-to-many domain proposals, not merged clusters. Profile domains are normalized before grouping, and very broad domains are excluded. Signals are a separately versioned derivation: deterministic cited profile facts, dated or numbered saved-note titles, and media types are merged with cited layout facts extracted from selected source passages for members of formed clusters. A note title's date is marked as a record date; publication dates do not count as event dates. This stage does not invalidate a saved profile or embedding. Cluster summaries are optional model annotations with source hashes; a changed member profile clears the annotation for review. Candidate pair retrieval routes through nearest persisted cluster centroids as an additional source while retaining global vector, lexical, concept, and explicit-link discovery.

## Run

Use Python 3.10 or newer. Run `uv sync --python python3.10` to install dependencies. No source snapshots or media are written to local disk.

```sh
uv run python -m mgraph migrate
uv run python -m mgraph backfill
uv run python -m mgraph project
uv run python -m mgraph enrich-web --limit 20
uv run python -m mgraph enrich-audio --limit 1
uv run python -m mgraph enrich-image --limit 1
uv run python -m mgraph enrich-pdf --limit 1
uv run python -m mgraph profile --limit 10 --model kimi-k3
uv run python -m mgraph embed --limit 10
uv run python -m mgraph relate --limit 5 --model kimi-k3
uv run python -m mgraph refresh-graph
uv run python -m mgraph enrich-signals --model kimi-k3 --limit 5
uv run python -m mgraph refresh-graph
uv run python -m mgraph annotate-clusters --model kimi-k3 --limit 5
uv run python -m mgraph status
```

`zsh run_parallel_profiles.sh` applies the pilot migration, screens fetched web identities, repairs saved primary names, refreshes stale Kimi judgments, and runs disjoint Kimi profile shards. It then repairs names again, audits every eligible current-version profile, runs disjoint Cloudflare embedding shards, refreshes judgments invalidated by new profiles, and runs disjoint Kimi relation shards up to 20,000 distinct pairs. Finally it persists clusters and neighbors, analyzes cited layout signals for multi-entry clusters in disjoint shards, rebuilds the graph, and annotates up to 40 clusters. Defaults are eight refresh, sixteen profile, four embedding, eight relation, and eight signal workers; `MGRAPH_REFRESH_WORKERS`, `MGRAPH_PROFILE_WORKERS`, `MGRAPH_EMBED_WORKERS`, `MGRAPH_RELATION_WORKERS`, and `MGRAPH_SIGNAL_WORKERS` set each stage independently. The audit stops downstream inference if any eligible profile is missing, stale, or has unsupported quotes, or if a web page has not been screened. The script resumes from versioned persisted projections. Kimi K3 profiling and identity screening default to `low` reasoning effort; set `MGRAPH_DO_PROFILE_REASONING_EFFORT` or `MGRAPH_DO_IDENTITY_REASONING_EFFORT` in `.env` to evaluate another effort level. Pair judgments use the model default unless `MGRAPH_DO_REASONING_EFFORT` is set. Run `.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`, inspect `mgraph status`, and manually compare sampled claims and property quotes with `read_memory` before restarting a large run after a profile change.

Run the prototype with `uv run python -m mgraph.map_server` and open `http://127.0.0.1:8765`. The overview shows persisted multi-entry clusters in a two-dimensional graph, with solid judged links and dashed embedding suggestions. Select a cluster to show its first 24 memories in the center and all ranked neighboring clusters in previews on both sides; selecting a preview changes the focus. A group picker filters the overview by persisted topic group and can include singleton clusters. Generic layout signals select graph, timeline, sequence, place, gallery, or place-plus-timeline arrangements. Place layouts currently show cited place labels, not geographic coordinates; a true map needs coordinate resolution. Unknown dates or order remain unplaced. Search still covers every projected entry, including entries without a profile or graph position. The saved graph updates through `refresh-graph`; rolling embeddings refresh it during a live backfill.

The Library tab pages authoritative DynamoDB source records by `node`, `file`, `link`, `collection`, `property`, and `linkTag`. On `node`, the `Profiled entries only` filter limits search, counts, and pagination to source records with a saved profile. Record details show raw source fields, associated root entry evidence, extraction output, profile concepts/tags/properties/claims, and embedding and pair-judgment status when available. The entry API also returns each extraction's identity status and reason; the Library continues to expose raw quarantined text for inspection, while MCP reads omit it. The library reads hosted PostgreSQL and does not download R2 snapshots or rerun inference. For a manual check, open the library, filter to profiled entries, search and advance a filtered page, inspect a profile, switch resources, then return to the map and open a multi-entry cluster. Verify that judged and suggested neighbors are labeled distinctly, select a neighbor preview, and use the group picker to browse a topic. The map is a pilot visualization, and overview coordinates are recalculated for the displayed set rather than being stable global coordinates.

The local MCP server runs over stdio with `/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/agent/experiments/mgraph/.venv/bin/python -m mgraph.mcp_server`. Use that absolute executable path and `-m mgraph.mcp_server` as arguments in an AI host's MCP configuration; no special working directory is needed. It exposes read-only `search_memories`, `read_memory`, `nearby_memories`, `compare_memories`, and `tabulate_memory_differences` tools. The last tool assembles persisted properties and cited claims side by side so an agent can answer comparisons without refetching source pages. Both in-process and subprocess MCP client calls passed. A connected agent can read the private one-user memory projection returned by these tools.

For hosts that accept the common JSON stdio shape:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "memotron-mgraph": {
      "command": "/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/agent/experiments/mgraph/.venv/bin/python",
      "args": ["-m", "mgraph.mcp_server"]
    }
  }
}
```

`--entry node:<id>` selects specific entries for enrichment, profiling, and embedding. `relate --left node:<id> --right node:<id>` judges a specific pair. Public page extraction can be partitioned with `--shard 0 --shards 4` through shard 3. Successful derivations are skipped on rerun; `enrich-web --refresh` fetches already processed pages again. An omitted `--limit` processes every eligible item and may entail substantial external API usage.

`zsh run_full.sh` runs the remaining public-page retry, Kimi K3 vision and profile derivation, Cloudflare embedding, and a first pass capped at 20,000 distinct Kimi-judged pairs across all restarts. Rerun the same script after a provider pause or process interruption: completed per-item derivations are skipped, and changed vision models invalidate prior image and scanned-PDF extraction hashes. The script reads the fixed DynamoDB snapshot already held in PostgreSQL and R2; it does not include later source edits.

After extraction, `zsh run_parallel_profiles.sh` screens page identity, refreshes stale judgments, runs disjoint Kimi profile shards, audits them, then embeds and judges pairs in disjoint shards. Relation budgets are computed from saved per-shard pair counts, keeping the 20,000-pair cap across restarts. Do not run it alongside `run_full.sh` or another profiling worker. It is safe to restart after interruption because screened pages, current profiles, embeddings, and current judgments are skipped. If screening or any shard exits unsuccessfully, the script stops before advancing to the next stage so the failed stage can be resumed deliberately.

During profiling, `zsh run_rolling_embeddings.sh` refreshes new embeddings in four disjoint Cloudflare shards, then rebuilds the saved cluster graph and waits five minutes. It exits when the profile workers stop; the backfill runner performs a final embedding and graph pass after its profile audit. This makes newly profiled entries available to the map while the long profile stage continues.

Profiling normally preserves a current profile even if a long entry required another model. Passing `profile --model <name>` explicitly recomputes profiles made by a different model; this is useful for model comparisons and can incur substantial inference cost.

DigitalOcean calls are sequential within each CLI worker. On HTTP 429 or 503, the client uses `Retry-After` and quota reset headers for bounded retries. If the indicated wait exceeds two minutes or repeated attempts fail, the command stops with `InferencePaused`; completed entries remain committed and a later rerun resumes them. Profile and relation inference release database reads before calling the model and retry atomic result/usage writes after a database restart without rerunning the model when the result was already committed. The client also checks the daily tokens remaining in successful response headers before the next request and pauses at `MGRAPH_DO_DAILY_RESERVE_TOKENS` (default 100,000), allowing for estimated prompt and completion tokens. This is a best-effort per-process guard because other account workloads and workers can consume the same allowance. Check live model-specific headers and observe 429s when changing worker counts. DigitalOcean's published Tier 4 ceiling is higher than the model-specific limits actually returned by the API.

`neighbors --entry node:<id>` returns the currently judged proximity order. User corrections can be recorded with `feedback-pair --left ... --right ... --score 0.9 --label same_niche` and `feedback-order --anchor ... --closer ... --farther ...`. Feedback is stored separately from model judgments and applied when returning neighbors. For a page that requires the authenticated Aside browser, pipe its extracted text into `import-text --entry node:<id> --source-node node:<id>`; this puts the text in R2 and the projection without making a local data file.

`python3 -m mgraph evaluate` runs four fixed synthetic relation cases against GLM-5.3 and Kimi K3 and writes `evaluation.json`. This checks JSON validity, evidence IDs, proximity ordering, latency, and token cost. It is a smoke test, not a labeled corpus evaluation. A user-reviewed test set from actual Memotron entries is still needed before treating the scores as accuracy measurements.

`python3 -m mgraph.evaluate_alternatives` runs the same synthetic cases against other DigitalOcean-hosted models and writes `alternative-evaluation.json`. Valid previous results are retained on rerun, so malformed outputs can be retried with a larger output budget without repeating successful calls. The comparison and whole-account cost scenarios are in `EVALUATION.md`.

The media extractor reads only S3 URLs in the configured user's legacy `tidyfiles` bucket. DynamoDB uses `MGRAPH_SOURCE_AWS_PROFILE`; file reads use `MGRAPH_SOURCE_S3_AWS_PROFILE`, which defaults to the DynamoDB profile. The available `data` profile passed a one-byte object read and is configured for this pilot. The extractor prefers an optional OpenAI-compatible Whisper endpoint on a DigitalOcean GPU Droplet when `MGRAPH_DO_TRANSCRIPTION_URL` is set; otherwise it uses Cloudflare Workers AI Whisper Large V3 Turbo with voice activity filtering. Large audio files are decoded with FFmpeg in memory and transcribed in four-minute chunks; this path requires `ffmpeg` on `PATH`. The DO serverless model catalog currently has no dedicated transcription endpoint. Image-only PDFs fall back to in-memory page rendering and DigitalOcean vision OCR for documents up to 20 pages. Existing transcripts and source metadata are also indexed.

Extraction has visible bounds: 260,000 characters for an HTML page, 100 pages and 260,000 characters for selectable PDF text, 20 pages for scanned PDF OCR, 80 MB for audio, and 30 MB for each PDF or image. Large raster images and GIF first frames are resized in memory before vision inference. Oversized sources keep their metadata in the R2 DynamoDB snapshot and their original bytes in legacy S3; each gets an `extraction_failure` row. Two earlier 80,000-character extracts that were found to be incomplete are marked `partial` and excluded from profiling and rich-evidence counts. Three saved PDFs are 262, 274, and 613 pages; they need a separate book-scale chapter projection before their full text can be profiled without losing coverage. Voice activity filtering can return no words on very short or non-speech audio, which is recorded as an empty-extraction failure.

## Pilot validation

The September 27, 2026 source backfill stored 37,917 records across 80 R2 pages; PostgreSQL record count and page row totals match. The root resolver handles the legacy `$NONE` sentinel, reciprocal page/clip references, and missing parent nodes; the corrected projection contains 5,017 top-level entries. R2 page 20 passed a decompression and SHA-256 check. A source audit found four formerly shortened blocks across three entries; all three were reprojected with full source text and profiled. Public-page extraction covered 2,302 of 2,551 web nodes. Media extraction recorded 235 image, 24 audio, and 26 PDF results; one web and one PDF result are marked partial and excluded from profiles. There are 250 web, 11 image, 21 audio, and 5 PDF failure rows, including records that overlap those partial results. The `data` AWS profile read legacy file objects, and saved audio, image, and PDF passed the complete S3-to-R2 extraction path. The inference sample has 69 profiles, 69 embeddings, and 53 judged relations, all current against their profile evidence. A full map of all 5,017 entries still requires a larger inference run. In one cross-medium sample, a saved Markdown entry and a web page received a `same_niche` relation at 0.72, while two high-vector-similarity pairs were judged 0.05 and 0.08; this is a concrete check of the candidate-and-judge split, not an accuracy benchmark.

## Configuration

Fill the remaining blanks in the ignored `.env` in this directory. `.env.example` documents every setting. Do not put credentials in the example file.

- `MGRAPH_DATABASE_URL`: a hosted PostgreSQL connection string with TLS. Use a dedicated database or schema; the provider must support `pgvector`.
- `MGRAPH_DO_MODEL_ACCESS_KEY`: a DigitalOcean serverless inference model access key. The listed reasoning and vision models are starting choices to benchmark.
- `MGRAPH_DO_PROFILE_REASONING_EFFORT` and `MGRAPH_DO_IDENTITY_REASONING_EFFORT`: reasoning effort for Kimi profile extraction and selective web identity judgments; both default to `low` in the pilot. `MGRAPH_DO_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` bounds each model request.
- `MGRAPH_DO_PROFILE_MODEL`, `MGRAPH_DO_RELATION_MODEL`, and `MGRAPH_DO_VISION_MODEL`: select Kimi K3 for profiles, pair judgments, and image understanding in the full pilot. The earlier GLM and Nemotron results remain in the evaluation history.
- `MGRAPH_CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `MGRAPH_CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_AI_API_TOKEN`: Workers AI REST access for embeddings and transcription.
- `MGRAPH_R2_BUCKET`, `MGRAPH_R2_ENDPOINT`, `MGRAPH_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, and `MGRAPH_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`: a private bucket and bucket-scoped S3 API credentials with object read/write access. R2 credentials are distinct from the Workers AI token.
- `MGRAPH_SOURCE_AWS_PROFILE`, `MGRAPH_SOURCE_S3_AWS_PROFILE`, `MGRAPH_SOURCE_AWS_REGION`, `MGRAPH_SOURCE_DYNAMODB_TABLE`, and `MGRAPH_SOURCE_USER_ID`: identify the read-only source and its separate file-read identity.

For the standard R2 jurisdiction, the endpoint is `https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`. A jurisdictional bucket needs its matching endpoint. Keep the bucket private. The backfill will use account-scoped object keys beneath `MGRAPH_R2_PREFIX` and keep object hashes and job checkpoints in PostgreSQL.

## Provisioned Cloudflare resource

The 21n Cloudflare account has a dedicated `mgraph-pilot` R2 bucket in the APAC location. Its `r2.dev` public URL is disabled and it has no custom domains. The account ID, bucket, endpoint, and user-scoped object prefix are already set in the local `.env`.

The local `.env` contains a [bucket-scoped R2 Object Read & Write S3 key pair](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/api/tokens/) for `mgraph-pilot` and a separate [Workers AI API token](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/get-started/rest-api/). The R2 user token expires on September 27, 2027.

## Connection checks

The hosted database schema was also tested by applying the migration to a rolled-back scratch schema. The source snapshot and extraction artifacts are stored in private R2, not on local disk.

# m graph pilot

Local development lives here. The pilot reads one user's legacy Memotron data from DynamoDB, stores derived graph records in hosted PostgreSQL, and stores source snapshots and extraction artifacts in a private Cloudflare R2 bucket. The loopback-only cluster map and local MCP server consume the same projection.

## Pipeline

The source stage reads only the six Memotron partitions (`node`, `file`, `link`, `collection`, `property`, `linkTag`) for the configured user. Each DynamoDB query page becomes a compressed, hashed R2 object and is upserted into the dedicated PostgreSQL schema. Page checkpoints make interrupted runs resumable. The source partitions are not a transactional point-in-time snapshot. A later catch-up generation is needed to incorporate edits after this completed backfill.

The projection stage identifies top-level entries, treats the legacy `$NONE` reference sentinel as empty, resolves reciprocal page/clip references, and folds child blocks into cited evidence without shortening source blocks or dropping descendants. Public-page HTML, owned file media, profiles, embeddings, and pair judgments are separately versioned derivations. An entry's source hash and each derivation's source hash determine whether it needs recomputation. Raw fetched page and media bytes go to R2; PostgreSQL holds searchable text, structured profiles, a 1,024-dimensional pgvector projection, and relation judgments. Before profiling, a resumable web-identity screen compares each fetched page with the saved title, URL, and description. Obvious matches are accepted; title conflicts, private-page URLs, and login fallbacks receive a Kimi judgment. Conflicting or uncertain page text is quarantined from profiling, search, and MCP reads while the original saved record remains available. The screen deletes any affected derived profile, embedding, and pair judgments so they can be regenerated from accepted evidence. Profiling splits each source block and accepted extraction into overlapping passages of at most 2,800 characters, packs complete passages into model requests, and reconciles long-entry summaries and uncertainty. Claims and property facts carry an entry ID, passage ID, and exact supporting quote; a validator removes facts whose quote does not occur in that passage. The saved title is the single primary `name`; other cited names remain in property facts. Property facts retain confidence and extraction observation time, and common property aliases are normalized for comparison. Entries needing more than 64 model requests raise a visible error. The legacy vector DataFn schema is unused.

Candidate relations are the union of vector neighbors, lexical matches, explicit links, and shared extracted concepts. DO reasoning judges candidates and persists a 0-1 proximity score, relation type, explanation, and supporting entry IDs. The evidence profile captures concepts, tags, properties, claims, and uncertainty for later chat and comparison surfaces. Thin title-only records remain marked `thin` and should not be treated as fully understood.

The cluster stage persists every profiled entry in a stable cluster identity. Strong judged links at or above 0.80 form current components; judged cross-cluster links at or above 0.65 remain separate neighbor edges. Embedding centroids provide explicitly labeled suggestions when no judged link is available. The projection retains cluster identities by member overlap across rebuilds and stores membership, multiple neighbors, topic groups, and generic arrangement metadata. Groups are many-to-many domain proposals, not merged clusters. Profile domains are normalized before grouping, and very broad domains are excluded. Signals are a separately versioned derivation: deterministic cited profile facts, dated or numbered saved-note titles, and media types are merged with cited layout facts extracted from selected source passages for members of formed clusters. A note title's date is marked as a record date; publication dates do not count as event dates. This stage does not invalidate a saved profile or embedding. Cluster summaries are optional model annotations with source hashes; a changed member profile clears the annotation for review. Candidate pair retrieval routes through nearest persisted cluster centroids as an additional source while retaining global vector, lexical, concept, and explicit-link discovery.

## Run

`zsh run_parallel_profiles.sh` applies the pilot migration, screens fetched web identities, repairs saved primary names, refreshes stale Kimi judgments, and runs disjoint Kimi profile shards. It then repairs names again, audits every eligible current-version profile, runs disjoint Cloudflare embedding shards, refreshes judgments invalidated by new profiles, and runs disjoint Kimi relation shards up to 20,000 distinct pairs. Finally it persists clusters and neighbors, analyzes cited layout signals for multi-entry clusters in disjoint shards, rebuilds the graph, and annotates up to 40 clusters. Defaults are eight refresh, sixteen profile, four embedding, eight relation, and eight signal workers; `MGRAPH_REFRESH_WORKERS`, `MGRAPH_PROFILE_WORKERS`, `MGRAPH_EMBED_WORKERS`, `MGRAPH_RELATION_WORKERS`, and `MGRAPH_SIGNAL_WORKERS` set each stage independently. DigitalOcean calls are sequential within each CLI worker. On HTTP 429 or 503, the client uses `Retry-After` and quota reset headers for bounded retries. ## Pilot validation

The September 27, 2026 source backfill stored 37,917 records across 80 R2 pages; PostgreSQL record count and page row totals match. The root resolver handles the legacy `$NONE` sentinel, reciprocal page/clip references, and missing parent nodes; the corrected projection contains 5,017 top-level entries. R2 page 20 passed a decompression and SHA-256 check. A source audit found four formerly shortened blocks across three entries; all three were reprojected with full source text and profiled. Public-page extraction covered 2,302 of 2,551 web nodes. Media extraction recorded 235 image, 24 audio, and 26 PDF results; one web and one PDF result are marked partial and excluded from profiles. There are 250 web, 11 image, 21 audio, and 5 PDF failure rows, including records that overlap those partial results. The `data` AWS profile read legacy file objects, and saved audio, image, and PDF passed the complete S3-to-R2 extraction path. The inference sample has 69 profiles, 69 embeddings, and 53 judged relations, all current against their profile evidence. A full map of all 5,017 entries still requires a larger inference run. In one cross-medium sample, a saved Markdown entry and a web page received a `same_niche` relation at 0.72, while two high-vector-similarity pairs were judged 0.05 and 0.08; this is a concrete check of the candidate-and-judge split, not an accuracy benchmark.

    wait "$worker_pid" || failed=1
  done
  if (( failed != 0 )); then

    return 1
  fi
}

print "m graph stage: Cloudflare embeddings, $embedding_workers disjoint shards"

class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    """Serve static map assets and read-only hosted graph projections."""
    def log_message(self, format, *args):
        """Avoid putting private search terms or entry IDs in access logs."""
        return

    def do_GET(self):
        if self.headers.get("Host", "").split(":", 1)[0] not in ("127.0.0.1", "localhost"):
            self.send_error(403)
            return
        parsed = urlparse(self.path)
        params = parse_qs(parsed.query)
        try:
            if parsed.path == "/api/map/clusters":
                self.send_json(query.map_clusters())
            elif parsed.path == "/api/map/graph":
                self.send_json(query.cluster_graph(params.get("limit", [180])[0], params.get("group", [None])[0]))
            elif parsed.path == "/api/map/focus":
                self.send_json(query.cluster_focus(params.get("id", [""])[0][:100], params.get("page", [0])[0]))
            elif parsed.path == "/api/map/entry-cluster":
                self.send_json(query.entry_cluster(params.get("id", [""])[0][:100]))
            elif parsed.path == "/api/map/cluster":
                self.send_json(query.map_cluster(params.get("id", [""])[0][:100], params.get("page", [0])[0]))
            elif parsed.path == "/api/map/groups":
                self.send_json(query.map_groups(params.get("offset", [0])[0], params.get("limit", [8])[0]))
            elif parsed.path == "/api/map/group":
                self.send_json(query.map_group(params.get("id", [""])[0][:100], params.get("page", [0])[0]))
            elif parsed.path == "/api/library/resources":
                self.send_json(query.library_resources())
            elif parsed.path == "/api/library/records":
                self.send_json(query.library_records(params.get("resource", ["node"])[0], params.get("page", [0])[0], search=params.get("q", [""])[0], profiled_only=params.get("profiled", ["0"])[0] == "1"))
            elif parsed.path == "/api/library/record":
                self.send_json(query.library_record(params.get("resource", ["node"])[0], params.get("id", [""])[0][:200]))
            elif parsed.path == "/api/search":
                self.send_json(query.search_entries(params.get("q", [""])[0][:200], 30))
            elif parsed.path == "/api/entry":
                self.send_json(query.get_entry(params.get("id", [""])[0][:100]))
            elif parsed.path == "/api/neighbors":
                self.send_json(query.neighbors(params.get("id", [""])[0][:100]))
            elif parsed.path in ("/", "/app.js", "/graph-view.js", "/style.css"):
                name = "index.html" if parsed.path == "/" else parsed.path.lstrip("/")
                content_type = "text/html" if name.endswith(".html") else "text/javascript" if name.endswith(".js") else "text/css"
                body = (ROOT / name).read_bytes()
                self.send_response(200)
                self.send_header("Content-Type", content_type + "; charset=utf-8")
                self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
                self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-store")
                self.send_header("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")
                self.send_header("Content-Security-Policy", "default-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'")
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(body)
            else:
                self.send_error(404)
        except ValueError:
            self.send_json({"error": "Invalid query"}, 400)
        except Exception:
            self.send_json({"error": "Graph query failed"}, 500)

    def send_json(self, value, status=200):
        """Send UTF-8 JSON without allowing cached personal data."""
        body = json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False).encode()
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-store")
        self.send_header("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

"""Contracts for cited layout signals and stable cluster identities."""
import unittest

from mgraph.cluster_pipeline import arrangement_for, entry_signals, normalized_date, stable_cluster_ids


class ClusterPipelineTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_publication_date_does_not_create_event_timeline(self):
        profile = {"property_facts": [{"key": "published_date", "value": "2026-09-20", "evidence_id": "a", "quote": "Published 2026-09-20", "confidence": "high"}]}
        signals = entry_signals(profile, "WEB_PAGE")
        self.assertEqual(signals[0]["role"], "publication")
        self.assertEqual(arrangement_for(["a"], {"a": signals})["primary"], "graph")

    def test_cited_places_and_event_dates_create_map_timeline(self):
        def profile(entry_id, day, city):
            return {"property_facts": [
                {"key": "event_date", "value": day, "evidence_id": entry_id, "quote": day},
                {"key": "city", "value": city, "evidence_id": entry_id, "quote": city},
            ]}
        signals = {entry_id: entry_signals(profile(entry_id, day, city), "NODULAR_MARKDOWN") for entry_id, day, city in (("a", "2026-09-01", "Taipei"), ("b", "2026-09-02", "Tainan"))}
        arrangement = arrangement_for(["b", "a"], signals)
        self.assertEqual(arrangement["primary"], "map_timeline")
        self.assertEqual(arrangement["ordered_entry_ids"], ["a", "b"])

    def test_cluster_identity_tracks_largest_overlap_after_growth(self):
        components = [{"members": ["a", "b", "c"]}, {"members": ["d"]}]
        ids = stable_cluster_ids(components, {"old-main": {"a", "b"}, "old-other": {"d"}})
        self.assertEqual(ids, ["old-main", "old-other"])

    def test_written_dates_keep_day_precision(self):
        self.assertEqual(normalized_date("January 04, 2025"), "2025-01-04")
        self.assertEqual(normalized_date("Published 2025-01"), "2025-01")

    def test_dated_note_and_numbered_title_are_generic_signals(self):
        dated = entry_signals({}, "NODULAR_MARKDOWN", "a", "January 04, 2025")
        numbered = entry_signals({}, "NODULAR_MARKDOWN", "b", "Chapter 6: The rise")
        self.assertEqual(dated[0]["role"], "record")
        self.assertEqual(dated[0]["value"], "2025-01-04")
        self.assertEqual(numbered[0]["kind"], "sequence")
        self.assertEqual(numbered[0]["value"], 6)
        self.assertEqual(arrangement_for(["a", "b"], {"a": dated, "b": dated})["primary"], "timeline")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
"""Focused checks for strong clusters and their neighboring evidence."""
import unittest

from mgraph.cluster_projection import neighboring_clusters


def edge(left, right, score):
    """Build one persisted pair shape for a projection fixture."""
    return {"left": left, "right": right, "score": score}


class ClusterProjectionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_judged_cross_cluster_link_precedes_embedding_estimate(self):
        edges = {
            "ab": edge("a", "b", 0.9),
            "cd": edge("c", "d", 0.84),
            "ef": edge("e", "f", 0.88),
            "bc": edge("b", "c", 0.72),
        }
        vectors = {"a": "[1,0]", "b": "[1,0]", "c": "[0,1]", "d": "[0,1]", "e": "[1,0]", "f": "[1,0]"}
        clusters = neighboring_clusters(edges, vectors)
        self.assertEqual([cluster["id"] for cluster in clusters], ["a", "c", "e"])
        self.assertEqual([cluster["size"] for cluster in clusters], [2, 2, 2])
        self.assertEqual(clusters[1]["neighbor"], {"basis": "judged", "score": 0.72, "pair_count": 1})
        self.assertEqual(clusters[2]["neighbor"]["basis"], "embedding")

    def test_visible_weak_link_becomes_two_singleton_clusters(self):
        clusters = neighboring_clusters({"ab": edge("a", "b", 0.7)}, {"a": "[1,0]", "b": "[1,0]"})
        self.assertEqual([cluster["size"] for cluster in clusters], [1, 1])
        self.assertEqual(clusters[1]["neighbor"]["basis"], "judged")

    def test_unjudged_and_low_scored_entries_are_not_plotted(self):
        clusters = neighboring_clusters({"ab": edge("a", "b", 0.2)}, {"a": "[1,0]", "b": "[1,0]", "c": "[1,0]"})
        self.assertEqual(clusters, [])
